Trump Administration officials on Tuesday announced that they would terminate the Obamacare coverage of 760,000 enrollees, alleging widespread fraud in enrollment.
Vice President JD Vance, who leads a White House task force aimed at eliminating fraud, said while speaking to reporters that $2.2 billion in taxpayer funds would be saved by removing the hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act (ACA) enrollees from the public insurance marketplaces.
“We expect that most of these people are fraudulently enrolled,” Vance said. He added that the Administration would also work to verify the eligibility of roughly 419,000 additional enrollees by ensuring that they are legal residents of the U.S. and meet the income threshold to receive Obamacare coverage.
The Administration will also place a six month moratorium on new health insurance brokers and agents, who help individuals sign up for health plans, Vance said.
Read More: Trump Pledges to Issue $500 Refunds to Nearly a Million Obamacare Enrollees. Are You Eligible?
The Administration’s move to eject fraudulent enrollees from the Obamacare insurance marketplaces is the latest in its broader efforts to crack down on fraud. An online “ledger” maintained by the White House asserts that the Vance-led anti-fraud task force has uncovered nearly $250 billion worth of fraud since Trump returned to office last January, including almost $100 billion at the Department of Health and Human Services.
That crackdown also saw the Administration pause $867.5 million in Medicaid payments to California and $199 million in Minnesota in July, an action for which Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. cited “suspected fraud and noncompliance.” Both states have pushed back on the claims.
The Administration has additionally targeted alleged fraud in food stamps , childcare facilities, COVID-era relief funding, student loans, and homelessness funding, among other areas. Critics have accused it of disproportionally focusing on Democratic-led states in its crackdown.
An analysis from the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) released last August estimated that 2.3 million Obamacare enrollees improperly claimed premium tax credits by intentionally overstating their income in 2025. The Trump Administration has also claimed that agents and brokers have been responsible for illegally enrolling tens of thousands of people in ACA plans.
The 760,000 enrollees now being removed from the ACA rolls by the Trump Administration represent about 4% of the estimated 19.2 million people receiving coverage through the marketplaces in 2026.
That total has sharply declined from its peak of more than 24 million last year as ACA premiums have surged following the expiration of subsidies that helped reduce costs for millions of enrollees at the end of 2025.
A poll conducted by health policy research group KFF in June found that most voters believe there is at least some fraud in government health programs, and that more than 70% feel it is an extremely or very important issue for candidates to discuss ahead of the midterm elections. For Republican voters, fraud topped all health care issues asked about in the survey, including costs.
But health care costs, which have become increasingly expensive in the U.S. in recent years, weighed more significantly for voters overall, and the poll found that only a minority of those surveyed believed that reducing fraud in government programs would reduce such costs for them personally.
Amid the Trump Administration’s moves to withhold millions in Medicaid payments, 71% also voiced the belief that preserving access to coverage through the insurance program was more important than rooting out fraud. Meanwhile, 65% believed that the Administration’s Medicaid payment deferrals were mostly politically motivated.

articles.title_orig: ICE officer in Texas shooting was recruit not using a body camera
articles.title_zh: 德克萨斯州枪击案中的ICE官员是未使用随身摄像头的新兵
articles.summary_zh: 新视频揭示了奥斯汀ICE枪击案发生前的追捕行动，但关键时刻仍未被发现
articles.content_orig:
AUSTIN, Texas — The ICE officer who shot a Venezuelan man in Austin on Sunday, leaving a bullet lodged in his back, was issued a body camera but was not wearing it during the shooting, two officials with the Department of Homeland Security told NBC News.
The officials said it was not clear why the officer was not wearing his body camera. Another ICE officer who was in the same vehicle was wearing a body camera, the officials said. That camera captured partial footage of the incident, but the footage does not include the moment of the shooting, the officials said.
Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, was shot early Sunday afternoon by an ICE officer while making deliveries as a DoorDash driver. He was taken to a hospital and, four hours after he was shot, was taken into immigration custody at the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall, Texas, his attorney said. The bullet remains in his back.
On Tuesday, a federal judge granted an emergency order temporarily blocking deportation proceedings against Garcés Pérez, according to his attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch.
The Travis County District Attorney’s Office also sent a letter to DHS and ICE leadership requesting that Garcés Pérez be allowed to remain in the country since he is “a material witness” in their criminal investigation into the shooting.
Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis shared on Tuesday evening some of the first video footage obtained by the department as part on their probe into the shooting. The videos came from an off-duty officer who captured part of the encounter between ICE and Garcés Pérez, as well as the sound of three gunshots, using his personal dash cam and cellphone.
After this, the off-duty officer alerted his colleagues to the shooting, allowing Austin police to quickly respond to the scene.
Davis said they are seeking the public’s help in obtaining any video evidence that can help them piece together the pursuit that preceded the shooting.
The day after he was shot, Garcés Pérez began “experiencing an inability to move his arm,” attorney Lincoln-Goldfinch said on social media. He was taken to the hospital Monday afternoon for several hours and then sent back to the detention center, she said.
The DHS did not respond to requests for comment about Lincoln-Goldfinch’s statements.
Earlier Monday, Garcés Pérez told a news conference via phone from detention that he was in a lot of pain and wasn’t getting the medical care he needed.
Lincoln-Goldfinch alleged in a social media post that after Garcés Pérez spoke out at the news conference, guards at the detention center “forcibly took the tablet from his hands, revoked his communication privileges, and moved him out of the infirmary into an isolated room with a flat bed that cannot be adjusted like a medical bed.”
He was then taken to the hospital around 5 p.m. after losing his ability to move his arm, she said.
“Wilber reports that he was handcuffed, shackled at the ankles, placed in a waist chain, and handled roughly during that transfer,” she said in the post.
Lincoln-Goldfinch said Garcés Pérez told her on Tuesday morning that doctors spoke to him about his care and gave him morphine for his pain.
“We now understand that the gunshot fractured his clavicle and that he has significant swelling and is wearing a sling,” she wrote. “We still do not have clarity about the cause or extent of the loss of movement he experienced.”
The attorney said Garcés Pérez was discharged from the hospital around midnight and taken back to the detention center, where he is receiving Tylenol and ibuprofen for his ongoing pain.
“He remains in isolation, on a flat bed, and without the tablet he previously used to communicate,” she said.
“We are asking for his communication privileges to be immediately restored and for him to be provided an appropriate medical bed and adequate medical care,” she said. “Most importantly, we are continuing to advocate for Wilber’s IMMEDIATE release.”
Rep. Joaquin Castro, D-Texas, said on social media that “despite losing movement on his left side and having a bullet lodged next to his spine, ICE has forced Wilber Rafael out of the hospital and back to the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall, Texas.”
He said that he and Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, would visit Garcés Pérez on Wednesday, check on his condition and demand his release.
A DHS spokesperson said in a statement late Sunday that Garcés Pérez was in stable condition and was in federal custody pending removal from the U.S.
A senior administration official told NBC News on Monday that Garcés Pérez did not have a criminal history beyond being in the country illegally.
According to Lincoln-Goldfinch, Garcés Pérez entered the country legally and was seeking asylum. She said Garcés Pérez had filed a change of address in immigration court, but received a notice to appear in court at the old address and never got it. Because he missed his immigration hearing, Garcés Pérez was ordered deported in absentia, according to his attorney.
On Monday, Lincoln-Goldfinch shared Garcés Pérez’s account of the shooting, saying he was making a delivery when “an unmarked black truck sideswiped him.” She said he didn’t know it was ICE as the truck chased him as he tried to make a U-turn, and then “pulled him out of the car.”
Previously, DHS has accused immigrants involved in shootings with ICE of using their cars as weapons while fleeing agents, without offering evidence of its claims. But it did not make the accusation in the case of Garcés Pérez or in the case of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, who was fatally shot in Biddeford, Maine, in July during a traffic stop.
ICE Director David Venturella previously told NBC News that every ICE officer and agent would be equipped with body cameras by the end of August, adding the agency would allow the “expedited release” of bodycam footage “when appropriate.” Further delaying that timeline is the possibility of DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin potentially switching or adding new vendors for body cameras.
A person who witnessed the aftermath of the shooting but who requested anonymity because he is going through immigration proceedings told Noticias Telemundo that he was waiting on customers at the ice cream shop where he works when he heard gunshots and ran outside, where he saw immigration agents surrounding a car.
“I approached the car and saw a man who looked sad and with his eyes full of tears. I asked him what happened to him, and he just told me, ‘I was shot in the back,’” said the person, a Mexican immigrant who has lived in the U.S. for more than two decades.
“You aren’t prepared to see someone like that. It makes you very angry, it pains you and you don’t know what to do,” he said.
A social media video verified by NBC News captures the sound of tires screeching followed by a person exiting a dark-colored SUV as a blue sedan is stopped next to it, both vehicles facing each other. The sedan appears to be damaged on the passenger side.
At least three gunshots are heard as the person approaches the sedan and runs up to it as it slowly lurches forward. The video shows the person standing next to the sedan’s driver’s side as it stops in front of an intersection.
Another video shows the blue sedan with its driver’s side door open and Garcés Pérez hunched over in the driver’s seat, holding his left upper chest, near his shoulder, as multiple law enforcement officers gather around.
The woman taking the video says, “Why did he do that to him?” The officers tell her that an ambulance is coming.
The video shows Garcés Pérez being taken out of the car and handcuffed behind his back. The agents make him sit on the ground. There appears to be a large bloodstain down his back. The officers cut open the back of his shirt, revealing a bullet hole.
An officer asks the woman taking the video if she saw what happened. In Spanish, she replies that “they just shot him because he didn’t want to stop” his vehicle.

articles.content_zh:
新视频揭示了奥斯汀ICE枪击案发生前的追捕行动，但关键时刻仍未被发现
得克萨斯州奥斯汀——新视频揭示了周日北奥斯汀ICE枪击案的筹备情况，尽管关键时刻仍然缺失。
奥斯汀警方发布了一段视频，显示ICE特工在枪击事件发生前与威尔伯·加西斯·佩雷斯的蓝色汽车在一起，以及随后执法部门的反应。然而，该视频不包括枪声或从最初停止到拍摄之间的10-15分钟。
相关| ICE参与北奥斯汀枪击案后，居民聚集在一起纪念
一名下班的奥斯汀警探恰好在附近，在进入附近的一家购物中心之前，用Garcés Pérez的个人行车记录仪在他的车辆附近抓获了ICE特工。据奥斯汀警察局官员称，在接下来的10到15分钟内，有一辆车在附近的街区被追赶，但该部门澄清说，没有证据表明有人徒步追赶。
奥斯汀警察局长丽莎·戴维斯说：“我们有一些视频，我们正在处理一段经过那里一些街区的追捕视频，并在那里结束。”。
警方表示，这段时间的视频是存在的，调查人员仍在努力收集和处理。目前尚不清楚的是，加西亚·佩雷斯为什么离开最初的交通站，沿途发生了什么事件，以及导致立交桥下发生枪击事件的原因。
Garcés Pérez的律师表示，她的客户报告称被一辆黑色SUV追赶，最初没有意识到这辆车属于执法部门。她说他正试图到达一个更安全的地方，而不是试图逃跑。
APD发布了关于北奥斯汀ICE枪杀委内瑞拉男子的视频
当休班的侦探回到车上时，他开始用手机录音，听到了三声枪响。现场第一名奥斯汀警察的随身摄像机镜头显示了枪击事件后的反应，但发布的视频中没有一段包括枪击发生的时刻。
加西斯·佩雷斯的移民律师凯特·林肯·戈德芬奇说：“我要求ICE提供行车记录仪录像，我不明白他们为什么不把它交给我们。”。
戴维斯警长表示，奥斯汀警方不知道被解雇的ICE特工是否佩戴了随身摄像头。截至周二的新闻发布会，该部门尚未要求联邦当局提供随身摄像头视频或类似材料。

articles.content_orig:
Hurricane Polo intensifies to ‘extremely dangerous’ Category 5 off Mexico coast
Category 5 represents the highest rank on the Saffir-Simpson scale, applied when wind speeds top 157 mph
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Weather forecasters warned that Hurricane Polo intensified on Tuesday and could strengthen further as the Category 5 storm moves alongside the southwestern coast of Mexico.
An advisory from the Miami-based National Hurricane Center described Polo as an "extremely dangerous" system featuring maximum sustained winds reaching 165 mph (266 kph).
Positioned 205 miles (330 kilometers) south of Zihuatanejo, Mexico, the cyclone was creeping northward at 2 mph (3.2 kph). Meteorologists at the center planned to deploy a reconnaissance aircraft to gather further data from inside the storm.
As Polo edged past the shoreline, officials in Mexico halted school sessions across several Pacific coastal districts.
Local populations remained anxious given that states such as Guerrero and Oaxaca are still recovering from destructive storms in recent years.
Forecasters cautioned that intense precipitation could trigger mudslides and flash floods.
Between 3 and 6 inches (8 to 15 centimeters) of rainfall is expected in Michoacán and Guerrero, while smaller totals may fall across coastal sections of Jalisco, Colima, and Oaxaca.
Current projections indicate Polo will stay out at sea, though high waves and tropical-storm-force winds are likely to impact coastal regions.
Category 5 represents the highest rank on the Saffir-Simpson scale, applied when wind speeds top 157 mph (253 kph).
Elsewhere in the Pacific, Tropical Storm Odalys was tracking well away from land with sustained winds of 65 mph (105 kph), with the hurricane center predicting it would reach hurricane strength on Tuesday.
Over in the Atlantic basin, Fay degraded into a tropical depression far southwest of the Azores, seeing maximum winds drop to 35 mph (56 kph) on Tuesday before turning into a remnant low later in the day.
No Atlantic hurricanes have developed yet this year, marking a record for the longest period a season has gone without one. Atmospheric effects from this year's El Niño continue to crush storms before they can intensify.

articles.title_orig: Trump Once Vowed to ‘Own’ Greenland. He Settled for Something Much Less.
articles.title_zh: Trump Once Vowed to ‘Own’ Greenland. He Settled for Something Much Less.
articles.content_orig:
Trump signs security agreement with Greenland and Denmark, but isn't 'complete' change
There are limits on Trump's claim of 'complete ability' to do what he wants.
President Donald Trump signed a security deal with the prime ministers of Greenland and Denmark on Tuesday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.
"This has been an amazing journey with tremendous people," Trump said of Denmark's Mette Frederikson and Greenland's Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
"This is tremendous for Europe and for the United States, for everybody, and for Greenland," Trump said. "It's going to be incredible, and the people of Greenland have been so nice. The people of Denmark have been amazing, and so I know it's going to be a long-term, fantastic relationship."
The agreement comes after months of escalating rhetoric from Trump, who has repeatedly threatened to take over the territory citing national security purposes. Trump's threats, including refusing to rule out taking the territory by military force, sowed tension between the U.S. and its European allies and sparked consternation from Greenlanders.
Greenland, which is an autonomous territory of Denmark, resisted Trump's calls to "take over" the island via acquisition or military force. Danish leaders said they were open to negotiating new frameworks for the U.S. military's presence, but that the sovereignty of the territory was a red line.
The text of the trilateral agreement reveals some red tape that constrains what Trump administration officials have billed as the "complete ability" to do what it deems necessary in Greenland.
While the deal appears to fall short of the "Complete and Total Control" by the U.S. that Trump once called for, it does grant the U.S. ability to expand its military footprint in Greenland.
The deal gives Greenland and Denmark the authority to review requests from the U.S. to build unmanned military installations "under accelerated governmental approval procedures."
Frederikson praised the agreement, saying that it was "bigger and better" than the deal struck with the U.S. in 1951.
"Seventy-five years ago, we entered into an agreement about the defense of Greenland. Today we are signing an even bigger and better agreement, a deal that can last forever," she said.
"Mr. President, you have been very clear. You don't want adversaries to come too close. I fully agree, and with this deal, they are not," she added.
Under the 1951 agreement amended by the new pact, the U.S. already enjoyed wide latitude to scale up its bases and military footprint on the island.
Nielsen acknowledged that the U.S. national security concerns are legitimate and praised the negotiation process that led to the agreement.
"The security landscape in the Arctic is changing, and we recognize the long term security threats that you, Mr. President, have rightly spoken about. It is for that very reason that we have insisted on engaging in a constructive dialog," he said. "Your security is our security, and our security is your security."
Nielsen called the agreement historic and a "win-win-win" for all parties.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte posted on X, "This agreement, along with NATO's growing role in securing this vital region, enhances our collective security and supports a safer and more stable future for us all."
In a post on his social media platform last Friday, Trump declared, "At my direction, we worked with representatives of Denmark and Greenland to guarantee that the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America."
The text of the deal affirms released Tuesday states that the U.S. can "modernize and expand its activities" at its existing Pituffik Space Base and says it can establish additional bases at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, following specific terms that the signatories had already agreed to.
If the U.S. wants to expand its footprint beyond that, the agreement requires that it puts forward a proposal that all parties will "immediately convene" to review via a standing committee that was established by an earlier memorandum of understanding.
If no agreement is reached within 90 days, the deal specifies that the proposal will then be elevated to the deputy minister level, and if that fails to the minister level -- secretary of state and equivalents. The text does not say what would happen if those consultations don't end in a consensus.
The deal gives Greenland and Denmark the authority to review requests from the U.S. to build unmanned military installations "under accelerated governmental approval procedures."
While the agreement details the U.S. military's right of free access to land, air and sea routes, it does not appear to materially advance privileges granted by the 1951 defense pact.
The agreement also bars non-NATO from establishing military installations in Greenland unless the three parties agree to make an exception.
The agreement also bans countries and individuals from countries that are either not NATO members or partners nor members of the European Union from having control or significant influence over "Particularly Sensitive Sectors" that includes critical infrastructure and the extraction of resources. The deal puts Greenland in charge of ensuring these prohibitions are upheld under its current or future investment screening laws.
The agreement specifies it has no end date and it plans for a contingency in which Greenland declares its independence from Denmark. An independent Greenland will agree to remain a member of NATO, athough that decision would likely not be entirely up to Greenland, the U.S. or Denmark -- joining the alliance requires the approval of all NATO members and an independent Greenland would have to go through the application process.

articles.title_orig: El Niño goes wild: Pacific Ocean under siege from tropical cyclones
articles.title_zh: El Niño goes wild: Pacific Ocean under siege from tropical cyclones
articles.content_orig:
A tropical storm off the south-west coast of Mexico has intensified into a category 5 monster in fewer than 24 hours, fueled by stronger than usual El Niño weather patterns in the Pacific Ocean.
Hurricane Polo was sending out maximum sustained winds of 165mph (266km/h) on Tuesday as its center churned about 215 miles (346km) south of the coastal city of Zihuatanejo, in Guerrero state.
On Monday, Polo was only a tropical storm with winds below 74mph (120km/h). Its rapid and sudden growth is testament to the dominance of this year’s so-called super El Niño, which set a record on Monday as the most extreme on record, and has amplified a number of extreme weather events globally.
Forecasters at the National Hurricane Center in Miami said Mexico was likely to avoid a direct hit, but warned that further intensification was likely, and that life-threatening flooding and mudslides were possible inland, along with dangerous surf and rip current conditions.
El Niño occurs when extended ocean temperatures in the eastern and central Pacific, and near the equator, rise above their historical average.
Meteorologists say the phenomenon increases disruptive winds and curtails other conditions favorable to storm development in the Atlantic basin, which remains quiet with less than three months to go in this year’s hurricane season.
Conversely, it promotes increased activity in the Pacific, where the 2026 El Niño remains one of the strongest on record.
“The water temperatures in two separate areas, the north-central Pacific and off the Mexican coast, are running well above average,” Paul Pastelok, AccuWeather’s lead long-range meteorologist, said in the online weather service’s fall hurricane outlook last month.
“We are seeing a strong impact in both the Atlantic and Pacific basins, with extreme wind shear limiting Atlantic storm development, while the Pacific remains quite active, as we expected back in the spring.”
Hurricane Polo’s single-day intensification also fits into the assessment of University of Miami senior research associate Brian McNoldy on his tropical Atlantic blog that El Niño, which he said was only “moderate” towards the beginning of September, was “forecast to become very strong, likely the strongest on record, by later this fall and into winter”.
Polo is the 18th named storm, and seventh hurricane, of the 2026 Pacific season, which runs from 15 May until 30 November.
By contrast, the Atlantic basin, which has a six-month season from June until November, has seen only six named tropical storms and no hurricanes so far.
It is the first time in 112 years that no Atlantic hurricanes have formed by 21 September, and 2026 could join 1907 and 1914 as the only years without one being recorded.

articles.title_zh: 法官就州检察官与派拉蒙华纳兄弟公司Discovery的和解举行听证会
articles.summary_zh: 一名联邦法官已定于周四就州检察长与派拉蒙华纳兄弟探索公司之间的拟议和解举行听证会。美国地区法官Araceli Martinez Olguin通过Zoom将听证会定在太平洋时间上午11点。她在周二的一份命令中写道，听证会将“解决有关各方拟议同意令的事实和法律基础以及拟议同意令执行情况的某些悬而未决的问题”
articles.content_orig: A day after Paramount Skydance and a group of state attorneys general announced a settlement clearing the way for its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, questions remain about whether the deal does enough to protect consumers and competition. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Oliver Darcy of Status. Geoff Bennett: A day after Paramount Skydance and a group of state attorneys general announced a settlement clearing the way for its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, questions remain about whether the deal does enough to protect consumers and competition. The $111 billion merger would create one of the biggest media companies in the world, bringing multiple film studios and cable channels, streaming services, and major franchises under one roof. It would also put two major news organizations, CBS News and CNN, under the same corporate umbrella. California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who helped lead the antitrust challenge before reaching the settlement, acknowledged he still has concerns about the merger. Rob Bonta (D), California Attorney General: This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger. It is not a blessing of the broader merger. Broadly speaking, we believe further consolidation in markets that are central to American economic life doesn't serve the American economy, consumers, or competition well. Geoff Bennett: But Bonta emphasized several key conditions of the agreement, including Paramount being required to release 30 films in theaters per year for the first two years, a $1.5 billion investment for homegrown film production, and the creation of an editorial independence board to support CBS News and CNN. The deal itself still needs to be approved by a federal judge. For more, we're joined now by Oliver Darcy of Status. Oliver, thanks for being with us. So what ultimately led to this settlement? Was it Ellison's threat to move Paramount out of California or something else entirely? Oliver Darcy, Founder, Status News: The threat from Ellison to move out of California seems to have loomed large over this. If you remember, Rob Bonta was calling this an illegal merger for some time and really vowing to go all the way with this and saying he was comfortable going to court. And something happened in the recent weeks. And that something is David Ellison was getting very serious about his threat to take production jobs from California and move them to maybe Nashville or to Texas. And you saw the governor, Governor Gavin Newsom, and local officials really worried about this and say they would like to see a settlement. And the pressure, from our understanding, reporting on this, was really great on Rob Bonta. He really needed to settle this to make sure that David Ellison left those Paramount production jobs and potentially the Warner production jobs in California. Geoff Bennett: Of all of the conditions attached to this settlement, which is expected to have the biggest effect on the entertainment industry? Oliver Darcy: Yes, I mean, a lot of this can have a huge effect on the entertainment business. I think that people are looking at the settlement that Rob Bonta got and not super thrilled with it. For instance, the big point about they have to release 30 films a year in theaters, if you look at the fine print, they do have to release 30 films, but they can co-produce half of them. So they only really have to release 15 films on their own, and then they can co-produce the other half and get those in the theaters to satisfy that requirement. Ultimately, Geoff, this is going to result in a lot of layoffs in the entertainment sector. And that's going to happen because there's going to be a lot of synergies between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount, the back offices, people who support communications and publicity, people who support H.R. jobs, legal jobs. Those jobs, I would imagine, would be almost immediately consolidated, and you're going to see a number of layoffs, and then it's going to just continue. This company that's going to be formed is going to be under billions of dollars in debt. They're going to need to find a lot of cost savings. And that's going to result regardless in a loss of jobs moving forward. Geoff Bennett: And Ellison has agreed to create this independent editorial board for CBS and CNN. But critics say what is described as a safeguard is in many ways hollow. Explain why. Oliver Darcy: Yes, there's a number of concerns here. One, usually, when you have an editorial board that's supposed to safeguard the CNN and CBS from management, you wouldn't have management get to select all the board members. In this case, Paramount gets to choose the five people who are going to be on this board. This board reports directly to Paramount's chief compliance officer. So, again, Paramount ultimately controls this board. It's unclear what power this board has. I mean, it doesn't say what power they have. If they find, for instance, that Paramount's management is interfering with editorial, what power do they have to remedy that situation? It's very unclear and not certain. This board also doesn't have to be formed for 180 days, meaning that David Ellison and company can, I guess, overhaul CNN, as they have overhauled CBS News, without having to deal with this board for the first six months or so. And so there are a lot of concerns this board is really just, as Kara Swisher, the CNN contributor and technology journalist, said, a fig leaf for management to get this deal across the finish line. It's something that Rob Bonta can hold up and say, look, we got this board that's going to safeguard CNN's editorial independence. But, ultimately, this board does not seem to have any real teeth. Geoff Bennett: And, Oliver, who actually polices all of this? How quickly could the states act if Paramount decides to start testing the boundaries of this settlement? Oliver Darcy: I mean, they theoretically have some avenues to enforce this. That's what Bonta wanted. And so, for instance, if they don't release 30 films a year, for each film they don't release, they're on the hook for I think $30 million or so. But, again, ultimately, this was not what Bonta was asking for. The state attorneys general, if you remember, they were asking for structural remedies, a change to the structure of this Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. And what they got ultimately were behavioral remedies, saying basically that Paramount will behave in certain ways moving forward. And that's not what they said they wanted. And so I think, when you look at whether it's the Writers Guild that's upset with this deal -- a number of critics, like Mark Ruffalo, who's been outspoken, said this deal was handing a win to oligarchs and Donald Trump supporters. If you look at why they're upset with this deal, it's because they basically didn't get anything that they wanted, and you're now allowing a deal which you had previously described as an illegal merger to go through. Geoff Bennett: Oliver Darcy of the media newsletter Status. Oliver, thanks again for your time. We appreciate it. Oliver Darcy: Thank you, Geoff.

一名联邦法官已定于周四就州检察长与派拉蒙华纳兄弟探索公司之间的拟议和解举行听证会。美国地区法官Araceli Martinez Olguin通过Zoom将听证会定在太平洋时间上午11点。她在周二的一份命令中写道，听证会将“解决有关各方拟议同意令的事实和法律基础以及拟议同意令执行情况的某些悬而未决的问题”
双方已提交动议批准同意令，该法令规定了一系列解决条件，以解决州检察官7月份提起的诉讼。其中包括派拉蒙承诺每年至少上映30部电影，以及另一项成立独立委员会监督CNN和CBS新闻遵守新闻标准的规定。
法官还取消了原定的听证会，即是否要求州检察官在诉讼进行时缴纳保证金。法官在另一份命令中表示，她将在“适当的时候”决定是否驳回美国作家协会为阻止合并而提起的诉讼。WGA表示，它还与派拉蒙达成和解，结束诉讼。

articles.summary_zh: 到目前为止，四分卫受伤一直是2026年NFL赛季的不幸故事。在第二周的训练营中，六名先发球员的缺席使联盟近四分之一的场上比赛黯然失色。幸运的是，许多伤病都是短期问题，只有轻微的破坏竞选的风险，但在少数情况下，几乎没有理由乐观。

articles.content_zh:
到目前为止，四分卫受伤一直是2026年NFL赛季的不幸故事。在第二周的训练营中，六名先发球员的缺席使联盟近四分之一的场上比赛黯然失色。幸运的是，许多伤病都是短期问题，只有轻微的破坏竞选的风险，但在少数情况下，几乎没有理由乐观。
纽约巨人队可能是六支失去首发球员的球队中最糟糕的一支。Jaxson Dart在“周一晚上足球”中膝盖受伤，经过进一步测试，伤势比球队最初担心的更严重。如果NFL的任何受伤的信号呼叫者错过了今年剩下的时间，Dart是最有可能的候选人。
如果这确实是达特的赛季结束，那么巨人队2026年的进球将发生巨大变化。对于其他球队，如西雅图海鹰队，即使面对伤病，人们的期望也基本保持不变。
以下是对所有六支四分卫受伤的球队的合理预期。
受伤球员：Jaxson Dart（膝盖）
新的期望：期待另一个早期选秀权
没有达特，巨人队的前景就没有糖衣了。（终于）激动人心的一年的所有要素都已经尘埃落定。在面对洛杉矶公羊队的比赛中，Jameis Winston替补上场，进攻看起来很倒霉，虽然这位老将过去有过不错的伸展，但他手臂力量的减弱、持续的失误问题以及与Dart相比他带来的机动性的大幅下降给巨人队带来了严峻的挑战。
在达特的核磁共振成像显示伤势比预期更严重后，温斯顿可能会在今年剩下的时间里担任进攻球员。自从达特作为首轮选秀权加盟以来，在没有达特的五场比赛中，巨人队以0比5获胜。这段历史表明，只要温斯顿是中锋，纽约将成为美国国家橄榄球联盟中最糟糕的球队之一。一线希望是，巨人队应该能够在2027年的选秀中为他们诱人的核心增加更多优秀的年轻人才，但这应该是一个该小组将他们从早期选秀范围提升到季后赛争夺的赛季。
受伤球员：Caleb Williams（腿筋），Tyson Bagent（脑震荡）
新的期望：陷入赛季初的洞，当威廉姆斯回归时爬出来
在第二周输给明尼苏达维京人队的比赛中，威廉姆斯被腿筋问题淘汰出局，最初看起来这将导致他长期缺席。相反，这颗冉冉升起的新星每周都在升起，甚至可能重新升起

纽约（WABC）-从2028年开始，航空旅客将首次获得此类航班服务……但要为长途旅行做好准备。澳航周二宣布，作为“日出计划”的一部分，澳航将于2028年年中开始开通悉尼和纽约市之间的直达航班，使其成为澳大利亚和大苹果之间有史以来第一条直达商业服务。这架18小时的航班将使往返澳大利亚的行程缩短3小时。
航班将由一架空中客车A350-1000运营，该飞机额外配备了一个20000升的油箱，可让飞机飞行16000多公里，近10000英里，不间断飞行长达22小时。澳航将总共接收12架飞机，每架飞机在四个客舱提供238个座位。纽约是继2027年10月开始的悉尼至伦敦直飞航班之后，第二条确认的日出计划航线。

articles.title_orig: Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson Explain Their ‘Brothers’ TV Idea — and What Happened at the Emmys
articles.title_zh: Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson Explain Their ‘Brothers’ TV Idea — and What Happened at the Emmys
articles.content_orig:
Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson play caricatures of themselves in Apple’s bizarre ‘Brothers’: review
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Add The New York Post on Google
Famous pals Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson play exaggerated versions of themselves in their new Apple TV comedy, “Brothers.”
It’s a messy stew of ideas that’s occasionally amusing. Mostly, however, the show is self-indulgent and aimless.
Premiering Sept. 23 on Apple TV, “Brothers” gets off to an irreverent start, as onscreen text informs us that it’s “based on a true rumor.”
In 2023, the “Dazed and Confused” actor revealed that he and Harrelson may have the same dad, convicted hitman Charles Voyde Harrelson. The former “True Detective” co-stars have never updated that claim with evidence.
In the show, the plot kicks off as Harrelson goes to stay at McConaughey’s ranch in Texas, bringing chaos to the latter’s relaxing life.
There, McConaughey’s mother (played by Holland Taylor) lets slip the explosive information about her past with Harrelson’s father. The “Cheers” alum then sets off to investigate her claim, which involves visiting dusty backwoods dive bars and dealing with bumbling criminals.
Harrelson’s subplot in the series is like “True Detective” mixed with “Dumb and Dumber.”
Meanwhile, McConaughey makes moves to run for the governor of Texas.
“Brothers” is several shows combined into one, and most of them don’t work. At times, it feels like a sly, backdoor way to announce a pivot into politics for McConaughey (the Texas native hasn’t announced a gubernatorial run, but he’s made past remarks that he’s open to it).
The show’s buddy comedy elements shine the brightest, such as scenes when the famously laid-back McConaughey is painted as “the uptight one,” compared to the even more aggressively mellow Harrelson.
But even that part of the story stumbles, too often aiming for low-hanging fruit to evoke laughs (such as a scene where the actors literally don fake noses and mustaches).
“Brothers” doesn’t seem to know what kind of show it’s trying to be.
It’s not a satire or a mockumentary. It’s not a sincere investigation of the rumor, or even the tried and true format of “celebrity pals travel around together in a docuseries.” It’s scripted, with actors in the supporting roles.
In the most baffling part of “Brothers,” Harrelson and McConaughey’s real wives (Laura Louie and Camila Alves) aren’t in the show, but the actresses (Brittany Ishibashi and Natalie Martinez) bear passing resemblances to them.
The same goes for their teenage kids, who get too much real estate in the plot. Nobody is tuning into this show to watch the superstar’s fake kids attend a school dance. Yawn.
Akin to “Curb Your Enthusiasm,” which perfectly blended reality and artifice, McConaughey and Harrelson’s on-screen wives and children have fictional names.
Though with “Brothers,” the point of this bizarre stagecraft with funhouse mirror versions of Harrelson and McConaughey’s families doesn’t land.
“Brothers” isn’t clever enough to balance its “not quite fiction, not quite reality” tone. It needed to commit to one side of the equation.
If Harrelson and McConaughey wanted to play brothers in a comedy together, the show would have been better served if it leaned harder into fiction.
Alternatively, “Brothers” could have made a fascinating docuseries about the actors unpacking the history of Harrelson’s father.
For instance, the show “Men in Kilts” followed “Outlander” actors Sam Heughan and Graham McTavish as they traveled around Scotland, learning about its history while mocking each other. It would be an easy format for Harrelson and McConaughey to put their own spin on.
“Brothers” tries too hard to be clever, and falls flat.
It feels like watching somebody else’s home videos from their childhood. Clearly, it’s entertaining for them. But to everyone else, it’s a mixture of dull, meandering, and confounding, sprinkled with occasional amusing moments.
“Brothers” premieres September 23 on Apple TV, with new episodes out weekly.

articles.summary_zh: 法医报告确认36岁的女演员帕内蒂耶雷死于多种处方药和芬太尼导致的意外过量，她在死前数周刚离开康复机构。
articles.content_orig: By — Jeffrey Collins, Associated Press Jeffrey Collins, Associated Press Share Copy URL https://www.pbs.org/newshour/arts/hayden-panettiere-died-from-accidental-overdose-involving-fentanyl-coroner-says Email Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Tumblr Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Hayden Panettiere died from accidental overdose involving fentanyl, coroner says Arts Sep 22, 2026 1:47 PM EDT Actor Hayden Panettiere died from an accidental overdose of several drugs, including fentanyl, a coroner in South Carolina said Tuesday. Panettiere, 36, was found unresponsive in an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, on Aug. 16. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the home. According to a statement from the Greenville County Coroner's Office, a combination of fentanyl and its chemical byproduct, as well as the anti-anxiety medication alprazolam, a muscle relaxer and a drug used to treat major depression and other serious mental health disorders, was found in Panettiere's system. The office did not include further details from the autopsy report in its initial release. Asked for comment on the coroner's report, Kasey Kitchen, a publicist for the family, told The Associated Press that "the investigation is still ongoing and the case is complex." Greenville Police confirmed Tuesday that their investigation into Panettiere's death is continuing. Paramedics responded to Panettiere's apartment last month after a 911 call and performed CPR and other advanced resuscitation efforts for more than 40 minutes before she was declared dead. An autopsy found no signs of trauma that could have contributed to her death, Greenville County Coroner Mike Ellis said in a statement. The police report released after her death listed medications Panettiere was taking, but the drug names were redacted. Panettiere's early fame brought success and struggle Panettiere soared to fame in the TV shows "Heroes" and "Nashville." In her memoir "This Is Me," released in May, Panettiere described lifelong scars from her early fame and acknowledged being addicted to alcohol and enduring postpartum depression after the birth of her daughter, Kaya, with Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko in 2014. She also endured family struggles and tragedy. Her parents' marriage was strained and eventually ended. Her younger brother, Jansen Panettiere, who was also an actor, died of a heart condition in 2023, at age 28. Panettiere also talked about her long relationship with Brian Hickerson and allegations that the aspiring actor physically abused her. WATCH: Remembering the life and career of Hayden Panettiere He was charged in 2020 with multiple counts of felony abuse, and he pleaded no contest to two counts of injuring a spouse or partner and served a short time in jail due to the case. He was sentenced to four years of probation and anger management and Alcoholics Anonymous sessions. Hickerson completed the terms and recently asked a judge to reduce his conviction to misdemeanors; that request was denied. Panettiere was one of two children born to Skip Panettiere, a former New York City fire captain, and Lesley Vogel, a former soap opera star. She acted in commercials and soap operas, including as the ever-troubled Lizzie Spaulding on "Guiding Light." In "This Is Me," she wrote that the traumas her character endured, from being kidnapped to killing her mother's boyfriend, led her to associate "catastrophe with adoration." She then played a cheerleader with supernatural powers in "Heroes," which propelled her to fame in 2006. By 2015, Panettiere was playing a brash country upstart opposite Connie Britton on "Nashville," which aired on ABC for four seasons before being canceled and revived on CMT. She did her own singing in the show, which scored some hits on country charts, spawned U.S. tours and earned Panettiere two supporting actress Golden Globe nominations. But she also said she was in a horrible cycle of using alcohol and drugs to battle depression and anxiety and had to find a way out of the darkness. She entered rehab while filming the show. "I was the one who put myself in the first treatment center. I was drowning," she said in a 2023 interview with Women's Health magazine. A free press is a cornerstone of a healthy democracy. 美联社：报告显示海登·帕内蒂耶雷在过量死亡前数周刚从戒毒康复机构获释
南卡罗来纳州格林维尔（FOX Carolina）——美联社报道，海登·帕内蒂耶雷在过量死亡前数周刚从戒毒康复机构获释。
根据法医公布的结果，36岁的加州人帕内蒂耶雷死于涉及多种处方药和芬太尼的意外过量。
美联社报道，根据他们获得的法医报告，帕内蒂耶雷是由加州马里布的一家机构释放的。
法医称，由委员会认证的法医病理学家进行的尸检未发现任何导致创伤的迹象。
毒理学检测确定官方死因是以下物质的毒性作用：
- 4-ANPP（另一种芬太尼）
- 美索巴莫（肌肉松弛剂）
- 喹硫平（抗精神病药）
帕内蒂耶雷的死因被裁定为意外。死因和方式确定后，法医办公室行政结案。
警方调查继续
法医办公室在8月16日初次应急响应后，与格林维尔警察局启动了平行调查。帕内蒂耶雷被发现昏迷在贾德森磨坊阁楼公寓内，地址为701伊斯利桥路，她当时临时居住在那里。
调度员在下午约1:51接到911电话，报告一名女性心脏骤停。急救人员和EMS人员到达现场，启动了高级心脏生命支持措施。复苏努力未成功，帕内蒂耶雷于下午2:32被宣布死亡。
周二，格林维尔警察局表示，虽然法医报告是一个关键组成部分，但他们的独立调查尚未结束。
“我们的探员将继续跟线索、收集信息，努力解决此案。”该部门表示。
美国缉毒局（DEA）表示，为“保护正在进行的调查工作的完整性，DEA不就具体调查发表评论”。
FOX Carolina已联系帕内蒂耶雷和布莱恩·希克森的公关人员征求意见。

articles.summary_zh: 曾六次投票反对要求特朗普停止对伊战争的共和党参议员候选人阿什利·欣森，如今呼吁“立即结束”冲突以缓解民众生活成本压力。
articles.content_orig:
UNITED NATIONS — The Middle East will take center stage when world leaders open the U.N. General Assembly's annual debate Tuesday, with some of Washington's most important regional partners arriving in New York facing a question: What will the region look like after months of war with Iran, renewed Houthi attacks and an uncertain future for Gaza?
Leaders from Jordan, Türkiye, Qatar and Egypt are expected to address the Assembly during the annual General Debate, which begins Sept. 22. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is also scheduled to attend.
President Donald Trump is expected to meet Gulf leaders on the sidelines of UNGA to discuss the Iran conflict and the region's future. U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz told Fox News Digital that the administration wants to hear directly from Gulf leaders about their concerns, describing the meeting as an important opportunity for diplomacy.
TRUMP WELCOMES NETANYAHU TO WHITE HOUSE AS RAGING IRAN WAR THREATENS TO SOUR US-ISRAEL RELATIONSHIP
Rich Goldberg, a senior adviser at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital that the Iran war has fundamentally altered the region's strategic landscape, creating opportunities for new energy partnerships and closer cooperation between Israel and its Arab neighbors.
"The opportunity for regional integration and normalization works alongside energy infrastructure meeting the moment, the crisis of needing bypasses for Hormuz," Goldberg said.
He argued that a network of pipelines carrying Gulf energy overland to the Mediterranean, potentially through Israel, could reduce dependence on vulnerable shipping routes.
"We can make the Strait of Hormuz irrelevant," Goldberg said, describing potential energy links between Saudi Arabia and Israel, as well as routes connecting Qatar to the Mediterranean.
IRAN-BACKED TERROR GROUP’S LATEST TERRITORIAL GRAB THREATENS SECOND GLOBAL SHIPPING CHOKEPOINT
But the threat to regional energy supplies now extends beyond Hormuz. The Houthis' offensive along Yemen's Red Sea coast has raised new concerns over the Bab el-Mandeb, another critical maritime choke point. Washington Institute analysts April Longley Alley and Allison Minor wrote in a Sept. 11 analysis that the offensive had "shattered the status quo" along Yemen's western coast.
NETANYAHU REJECTS BOARD OF PEACE'S GAZA PLAN: NO 'WITHDRAWAL UNTIL HAMAS IS GENUINELY DISARMED'
Gaza presents a separate diplomatic challenge, with Arab governments seeking a political settlement while differing with Israel over Palestinian statehood and the territory's future.
In a Sept. 6 joint statement, the foreign ministers of Jordan, Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Indonesia and Pakistan rejected proposals to forcibly displace Palestinians from Gaza and reiterated support for a Palestinian state along the 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital. They also warned that displacement proposals risk undermining Trump's Gaza peace plan.
ISRAEL’S E1 PLAN EXPLAINED: THE JERUSALEM-AREA CORRIDOR SPARKING INTERNATIONAL BACKLASH
Qatar has simultaneously condemned renewed Iranian attacks against Arab states and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, while insisting that the Palestinian issue remains a priority.
In a Sept. 8 joint statement, the leaders of France, Britain and Canada announced plans to ban imports from Israeli settlements and pursue targeted measures against settlements and those who facilitate them. They also said they would co-chair a meeting during UNGA to advance a two-state solution, one year after recognizing Palestinian statehood.
The diplomatic divisions will also be reflected in who can address the U.N. in person. Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas was denied a U.S. visa for the second consecutive year. The General Assembly voted Thursday to allow him to deliver his address by video.
Netanyahu, meanwhile, is expected to travel to New York weeks before Israel's Oct. 27 parliamentary elections, the country's first national vote since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, amid declining international support for Israel. A June 2026 Pew Research Center survey found that a median of 67% of adults across 36 countries held unfavorable views of Israel, compared with 25% who viewed it favorably.
For Washington, the challenge is balancing its regional security relationships with competing demands over Gaza and the future of relations with Israel.
TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS
Goldberg predicted that some of the most consequential discussions would take place away from the General Assembly podium, with Arab leaders delivering one message publicly and another in private meetings with Trump and senior U.S. officials.
"We may see the old propaganda of criticizing Israel and saying everybody wants a different future, and they're going to support Gaza and the Palestinians, they demand a Palestinian state," Goldberg said.
Behind closed doors, he predicted the discussions would focus on U.S. security guarantees, the next steps in confronting Iran and expanding regional energy infrastructure.

"What will be a pathway forward politically that the U.S. can provide to these leaders so that they can normalize with Israel alongside the necessary infrastructure upgrades that they need to make for their own energy securities and physical securities going forward?" Goldberg said.

爱荷华州共和党众议员阿什利·欣森曾六次投票反对指示特朗普总统停止对伊战争的众议院决议，最近一次就在上周。

但周一，这位共和党参议员候选人呼吁“立即结束”这场冲突。

“爱荷华人正承受压力，不应该为伊朗战争在加油站和收银台买单，”欣森在X平台上写道，并呼吁采取暂停燃油税、暂停柴油出口、补充高速公路信托基金等措施来缓解高成本压力。

“这些降低成本的措施刻不容缓，这场战争需要取得胜利并立即结束，”她说。

她的民主党对手乔什·图雷克迅速作出回应，还指出欣森第七次投票反对结束美国在黎巴嫩敌对行动——这是中东冲突的一部分。

图雷克在回复欣森时于X平台写道：“发一条推文很容易，但当你有机会投票结束这场战争时，你却选择了不投。”

“你七次投票支持继续战争，包括就在上周。是时候真正结束这些永无休止的战争，把爱荷华州和爱荷华人放在首位了，”图雷克继续说道。“我很高兴你终于跟随我的步伐——此前我上周提出的应对伊朗战争成本上涨的提案，你曾犹豫不决。”

上个月，无党派的库克政治报告将爱荷华州参议院选情评级从“倾向共和党”调整为“胜负难料”。特朗普在过去三届总统选举中都赢下了该州，而民主党自2008年以来从未在该州赢得过参议院席位。

欣森的竞选团队未立即回应就其此前在众议院投票反对伊朗战争授权法案的置评请求。

最新决议上周二以220票对204票在众议院通过，七名共和党人加入在场全体民主党人的支持行列。其中两人是爱荷华州的扎克·纳恩和玛丽安妮特·米勒-米克斯，他们此前反对此类措施，但改变了立场。

两人都在摇摆选区竞选连任。库克政治报告将他们的选情评为“胜负难料”。

欣森是连任三届的众议员，随着民调显示选民不满总统对战争和经济的处理方式，她越来越将自己塑造为“两党合作”的形象，并逐渐与特朗普政府拉开距离。她的表态和投票凸显了……

articles.content_orig: President Trump took his “America First” foreign policy to the world stage, using his address to the UN General Assembly to defend the war with Iran and issue a stark warning to Iran's leadership. Trump said a deal could come after the midterm elections and that the alternative was to “annihilate the Islamic Republic.” Nick Schifrin reports. President Trump took his America first foreign policy to the world stage today, using his address to the U.N. General Assembly to defend the war with Iran and issue a stark warning to Iran's leadership. Mr. Trump said a deal could come after the midterm elections, and that the alternative was to -- quote -- "annihilate the Islamic Republic." The president's speech and several of his meetings today were broadcast by the U.N.'s TV operation, which is separate from the U.S. pool of TV networks that is suing the president over his ban of three news organizations. Nick Schifrin starts our coverage from New York. Nick Schifrin: Today, in front of global leaders whose countries have been hit by unprecedented attacks, food shortages and higher energy prices because of the U.S. Israeli war in Iran, President Trump defended his decision to go to war. President Donald Trump: They were the bully of the Middle East, but they're the bully no more. Nick Schifrin: And at the U.N., whose charter bans countries from threatening military force except in self-defense, President Trump delivered a threat. Donald Trump: Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations? But I believe we will make a deal right after the election, because it doesn't make sense for them not to. Nick Schifrin: For his part today, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran did not trust another negotiation, even though Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met today with U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Masoud Pezeshkian, Iranian President (through interpreter): We have been at the negotiating table several times. The whole world sees that they are easily trample on, the agreements. They cannot use force to compel people to submit. Nick Schifrin: But President Trump's threats of force against a NATO treaty ally led to today's agreement between the U.S., Denmark, and Greenland, which has been part of the Kingdom of Denmark since 1721. The deal allows the U.S. to add to its existing military presence with two new bases. NATO will boost presence in the Arctic, and the world's largest island will permanently ban Chinese and Russian investment without giving up Greenland or Danish sovereignty. Donald Trump: We're going to have a tremendous relationship, a secure relationship, and we look forward to it. Nick Schifrin: That's a turnaround from his previous threats disrespecting Danish sovereignty that threatened overall NATO cohesion. Donald Trump: And all we're asking for is to get Greenland, including right, title and ownership, because you need the ownership to defend it. You can't defend it on a lease. Nick Schifrin: But, today, Denmark and Greenland call this deal a win-win. Mette Frederiksen, Prime Minister of Denmark: The, day we are signing an even bigger and better agreement, a deal that can last forever. This deal is good for the United States. It's good for Greenland, for Denmark, for the NATO alliance, and therefore also good for Europe. Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Prime Minister of Greenland: This is not only an agreement about us, it is an agreement with us. It takes into account the people of Greenland, our rights, our livelihoods, and the development of our country. articles.title_orig: Sri Lanka Convicts 15 in Easter 2019 Bomb Attacks
articles.title_zh: Sri Lanka Convicts 15 in Easter 2019 Bomb Attacks
articles.content_orig:
Sri Lanka court convicts 15 men over deadly Easter Sunday bombings
Sri Lanka's High Court has given long jail sentences to 15 men charged with plotting the 2019 Easter Sunday bomb attacks that killed 270 people and injured more than 500.
Those found guilty include Naufer Moulavi, who prosecutors said masterminded the suicide bombings. Nine other men were acquitted.
The co-ordinated blasts at three churches and three luxury hotels were the deadliest in Sri Lanka since the end of its civil war in 2009. Forty-five foreigners were among the dead.
All the bombers who carried out the attacks died in the blasts. Investigators have previously blamed the bombings on Islamist extremists, and the 25 men indicted were from Sri Lanka's Muslim minority. One died in custody.
The 15 defendants on Tuesday were each given prison terms ranging from 200 to 260 years.
The court in the capital Colombo also ordered the confiscation of their all movable and immovable assets.
The accused, who had been charged with more than 23,000 offences, were handcuffed in pairs and brought to the court in two prison buses.
Most of those killed were Sri Lankans, many of whom were children.
They included celebrity chef Shantha Mayadunne and her daughter, an entire young family of five, at least eight members of staff from the hotels targeted and five members of the same family from the western Sri Lankan city of Negombo.
The foreigners who died included 11 Indians, eight Britons and five Americans.
Among the dead there were also citizens of Australia, Bangladesh, China, Denmark, Japan, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and Turkey.
Three of Danish billionaire Anders Holch Povlsen's children died in the attack on the Shangri-La hotel, while the family had been holidaying there.
In the wake of the attacks, Sri Lankan authorities pointed to a "major intelligence lapse". Its parliament heard that a tip-off from India about the attacks was not properly shared with the authorities.
In 2023, the Supreme Court ordered former president Maithripala Sirisena to pay millions in compensation to the victims of the bombings, after finding him responsible for national security failures that led to the attacks.
Last month, two former senior officials were sentenced to death for criminal negligence that led to the bombings. Death sentences are usually commuted to life in prison in Sri Lanka due to a decades-old moratorium on executions.
For years, Sri Lankans have held regular demonstrations demanding justice for the victims of the Easter attacks.
The verdict comes as a separate investigation into former intelligence chief Suresh Sallay is under way. Sallay is accused of orchestrating the bombings with Islamist extremists.
The allegations echo those aired in a 2023 documentary by British broadcaster Channel 4, which heard whistleblower testimony claiming the attacks were allowed to happen to boost the popularity of the Rajapaksa family, which long dominated Sri Lankan politics.
Sallay, who was arrested in February, denies the allegations. Former president Gotabaya Rajapaksa, who was elected months after the 2019 attacks, with a campaign of tackling Islamist extremism has also denied the allegations.
Rajapaksa, who has been banned from leaving the country, has asked the court to prevent his potential arrest in connection with the ongoing investigations.

articles.summary_zh: Xi的“专机”与空军一号相比如何？看看这位中国领导人的飞机，这一定会成为他华盛顿国事访问视觉编排的一部分中国领导人乘坐的这架飞机，在官方媒体和官方声明中经常被称为“转机”或“专机”，尽管两国都使用波音747进行总统旅行，但世界对它的了解仍远不及空军一号。
articles.content_orig:
How does Xi Jinping’s ‘special plane’ compare with Air Force One?
A look at the Chinese leader’s aircraft, which is bound to become part of the visual choreography of his state visit in Washington
The aircraft carrying China’s leader, often referred to in state media and official statements as a zhuan ji, or special plane, remains far less known to the world than Air Force One, despite both countries using Boeing 747s for presidential travel.
For a head of state, a presidential aircraft is more than a means of transport. Its range, on-board facilities and security systems reflect the practical demands of presidential travel and diplomatic missions, and the aircraft itself becomes part of the visual choreography of a state visit.
In one sense, it is one of the first symbols of a country to arrive in the host country, appearing in the sky before the president steps onto the tarmac.
articles.content_zh:
Xi的“专机”与空军一号相比如何？看看这位中国领导人的飞机，这一定会成为他华盛顿国事访问视觉编排的一部分中国领导人乘坐的这架飞机，在官方媒体和官方声明中经常被称为“转机”或“专机”，尽管两国都使用波音747进行总统旅行，但世界对它的了解仍远不及空军一号。
对于国家元首来说，总统专机不仅仅是一种交通工具。它的航程、机载设施和安全系统反映了总统旅行和外交使团的实际需求，飞机本身也成为国事访问视觉编排的一部分。从某种意义上说，它是一个国家抵达东道国的首批象征之一，在总统走上停机坪之前出现在天空中。

articles.content_zh:
北京--中国周二表示，它现在要求向美国、墨西哥和加拿大出口另外两种可用于制造非法药物的化学品，扩大了对向这三个国家运输的控制。
在中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周会晤之前，商务部和其他当局共同宣布了新规定。这些增加使受此类控制的化学品数量达到18种。
美国称中国是世界上许多用于非法生产芬太尼、甲基苯丙胺和其他致命合成药物的前体化学品的最大生产国。它敦促北京采取更积极的行动，减少不受监管的前体化学品的流动。
2025年11月，北京宣布限制向美国、加拿大和墨西哥出口13种“制药”化学品，包括用于生产合成阿片类药物的化学品，这些化学品每年在美国造成数万人过量死亡。今年5月，中国在清单上又增加了三种与芬太尼相关的前体。在采取这些措施之前，Xi和特朗普于2025年10月在韩国和5月在北京举行了会晤。
中国面临美国征收的芬太尼相关关税。北京随后于2025年3月发布了一份报告，详细说明了其控制芬太尼非法贸易的努力。中国外交部长还抨击美国以关税回应北京的善意。美国最高法院于2月取消了关税。

articles.title_orig: Trump tells U.N. he could ‘annihilate’ Iran but expects a deal after the midterm elections
articles.title_zh: Trump tells U.N. he could ‘annihilate’ Iran but expects a deal after the midterm elections
articles.content_orig:
In a speech to world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly, President Donald Trump defended the Iran conflict and said he was considering whether to “annihilate” the country and drive it “into hell.”
Or, he said, Iran could make a deal with the U.S. that would allow the nation to rebuild. But that won’t happen until after the midterm elections in November, Trump predicted.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”
Trump later said U.S. envoys met with Iranian officials for three hours on the sidelines of the gathering, an unexpected development that offered a glimpse of diplomatic activity.
But Trump has repeatedly floated new attacks on Iran, even previously threatening death to the entire civilization. On Tuesday, he revived that warning at one of the most prominent platforms for world leaders, with an Iranian delegation in the audience.
“I have a big decision to make,” he said. “Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”
“Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he continued.
Most important, Trump said to applause, is ensuring that “Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.”
Iran’s nuclear potential was “the reality we had to confront,” he argued, and “a reality that far too many preferred to ignore.” Tehran has insisted its nuclear program is for civilian purposes and denied having plans to develop nuclear weapons.
The U.N. assembly comes as the Iran war is about to enter its eighth month.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the U.N. on Wednesday. Trump told Fox News that he would “probably” be open to meeting with Pezeshkian but did not announce any specifics.
Trump also highlighted peace deals he has worked on, U.S. actions in the Western Hemisphere and progress on his 20-point peace plan in the Gaza Strip.
Trump’s remarks to the assembly this year come as the U.N.’s Human Rights Council found in a report last week “reasonable grounds to believe” that the U.S. had committed war crimes during “indiscriminate attacks” against an Iranian school and a residential area in February.
The American president traditionally addresses the General Assembly each year.
During his wide-ranging speech, the president said America is “doing better than ever before,” touting the U.S. economy and his approach to immigration and artificial intelligence.
Less than a minute into his remarks, Trump called the U.S. economy “the envy of the world” and pointed to his administration’s tax policy and stock market records.
“Our economy is the envy of the world,” he said. “Our military is the most powerful on Earth. Our technology is second to none, and we are leading in virtually everything.”
Many American voters, though, don’t appear to agree. An NBC News poll conducted in September found that 56% of registered voters disapprove of the job the president is doing, and 55% said they believe his policies hurt the economy.
Gas prices remain high, sitting at an average of $4.47 per gallon, about a 50% increase since the war with Iran began. Diesel prices also spiked, affected by the Iran war as well as the war between Russia and Ukraine. Diesel hit a record $6 per gallon earlier this month before surging higher to $6.52 as of Tuesday, according to AAA.
Later, the president touted his record on immigration, tying his crackdown on the southern border to a drop in violent crime in the U.S.
“The entire world is being lifted by the wealth, strength, spirit and momentum of a newly energized and a very powerful United States of America,” he said.
While Trump declined to endorse guardrails on artificial intelligence, he did push for one change: its name.
Trump said the U.S. would refer in official documents to “superintelligence,” rather than “artificial intelligence.” The word “artificial,” Trump argued, “makes it sound fake, and it is not fake. It’s actually amazing.”
Earlier this month, industry insiders warned that artificial intelligence could lead to human extinction, potentially in the next decade.
Trump said Tuesday that he would not “stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution.”
“We’re going to encourage it, not rein it in,” he said. “We’re going to watch it closely through the Department of Justice.”
Trump has previously said that the only guardrail the U.S. needs is “a STRONG AND SMART” president.
Artificial intelligence is also expected to be a main topic of conversation during Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week.
Greenland, Ukraine and Venezuela
Trump met with several world leaders on the sidelines of the U.N. gathering, including Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez. It was Rodríguez’s first meeting with Trump since the U.S. captured then-Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, who are in a Brooklyn, New York, jail, awaiting trial.
Weeks ago, Trump said that the U.S. entered an agreement with Venezuela for U.S. majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of oil reserves in Venezuela.
On Tuesday, Trump called it “perhaps the biggest deal ever made,” adding: “To the victor belong the spoils.”
Trump said the Venezuela raid was “proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere,” noting U.S. attacks on drug cartels before pivoting to Cuba.
“My administration is seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba,” he said, adding, “It will fall.”
In response, the Cuban delegation stood up and left the assembly hall.
Later Tuesday, Trump met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said: “I hope that we will end this war, and President Trump will help us help us end this war,” Zelenskyy said.
Trump said during his speech that the war in Ukraine would end “more quickly than people understand.”
For years, the president said he would end the war. During his 2024 presidential campaign, he said he could end the war within 24 hours or even before his presidency began.
Last week, Trump signed into law a Russian sanctions bill championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C.
He also announced that the U.S. would take over military operations and have “permanent control over security” in Greenland, in a deal signed later Tuesday with the leaders of Greenland and Denmark to try to end the tense standoff over the strategic Arctic territory.

articles.title_orig: Taiwan is watching closely as Xi and Trump meet and hopes US will keep up its arms sales
articles.title_zh: Taiwan is watching closely as Xi and Trump meet and hopes US will keep up its arms sales
articles.content_orig:
TAINAN, Taiwan (AP) — As China’s Xi Jinping arrives in Washington to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump, Taiwan expressed confidence that U.S. arms sales to the island that Beijing claims as its own will continue — despite China’s pressure.
China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a summit in May between Trump and Xi in Beijing. After that meeting, the United States paused the sale of a record-breaking $14 billion package — and Trump described arms sales to Taiwan as a “very good negotiating chip” with China.
Still, the U.S. government and Congress have “repeatedly expressed support for Taiwan’s self-defense capabilities,” Taiwanese Defense Ministry spokesperson Maj. Gen. Chiao Fu-chun told reporters in the southern city of Tainan.
“We will continue to maintain close contact with the U.S. Department of War and continue to push forward the arms procurement deal between Taiwan and the U.S., ensuring it proceeds as planned,” he added.
The U.S. is bound by its own laws to provide Taiwan — a self-ruled democracy that China sees as its own territory — with the means to defend itself. While not recognizing Taiwan as a country, the U.S. is the island’s strongest informal backer and arms provider.
Washington approved another $11 billion package for Taiwan in December.
Hours before Xi’s arrival for the three-day state visit to the U.S., Taiwan’s military on Wednesday conducted live fire drills featuring a domestically developed eight-wheeled armored vehicle, highlighting efforts to strengthen its own arms production.
Called The Cheetah, the vehicle can be fitted with a 105-millimeter (4.1-inch) cannon and can reach a maximum speed of about 100 kph (62 mph) and an operational range of about 500 kilometers (311 miles).
Taiwanese Maj. Gen. Chen Chien-chung said the vehicle can be used on various terrains and is suitable for urban warfare.
Trump has in recent years pressed Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te to dramatically increase Taiwan’s defense budget. The budget will exceed 3% of Taiwan’s gross domestic product for the first time in 2027, and Lai has pledged to get to 5% by 2030.
Mistreanu reported from Taipei, Taiwan.

articles.title_zh: Digital yuan speeds up as Ant International spurs instant cross-border transfers
articles.content_orig:
Chinese banks, Ant International push instant cross-border digital yuan transfers
The Shanghai-to-Hong Kong settlements worth hundreds of millions of yuan bypassed traditional channels and could accelerate Beijing’s broader yuan strategy
Two Chinese state-owned banks and Ant International have trialled cross-border digital yuan transfers worth hundreds of millions of yuan, marking the latest step in Beijing’s efforts to streamline settlements and promote wider international use of the digital yuan.
The Shanghai branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) facilitated its first digital yuan transfer for Ant International to ICBC Asia, its Hong Kong subsidiary. The transaction from Shanghai to Hong Kong was completed within seconds, compared with the several days typically required for large cross-border transfers through traditional channels, domestic media outlet Financial News reported on Tuesday.
Ant International is the Singapore-based arm of China’s Ant Group, an affiliate of Alibaba, which owns the South China Morning Post.
Similarly, the Shanghai branch of China Construction Bank (CCB) also facilitated a digital yuan transfer worth hundreds of millions of yuan for Ant International to CCB Asia, the bank’s Hong Kong subsidiary, state-owned China Business Journal reported on Friday.

articles.title_orig: China's Xi kicks off state visit to Washington on Wednesday with a rare planeside welcome from Trump - ABC News
articles.title_zh: China's Xi kicks off state visit to Washington on Wednesday with a rare planeside welcome from Trump - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
China's Xi kicks off state visit to Washington on Wednesday with a rare planeside welcome from Trump
When Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington, he’s expected to get a rare greeting from President Donald Trump, who will be on the tarmac to welcome his counterpart’s plane instead of waiting for him to drive up to the White House
WASHINGTON -- When Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington on Wednesday, he's expected to get a rare greeting from President Donald Trump, who will be on the tarmac to welcome his counterpart's plane instead of waiting for him to drive up to the White House.
Trump's decision to greet Xi at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington rather than receiving him at the executive residence shows how far the U.S. president is going to honor China's leader as he makes his first state visit in more than a decade.
The White House has not released many details about Wednesday's greeting, but Trump is expected to participate in an arrival ceremony at the base with Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan. The salutation will kick off a three-day visit that's expected to be saturated with pomp, even by White House standards. The state visit, complete with a formal state dinner at the White House on Thursday, is supposed to reciprocate for the ceremonial grandeur that marked Trump's May visit to China.
But it's also a showy patina at a time when tensions between the two geopolitical rivals are high over trade, artificial intelligence, Trump's war with Iran and China's designs on Taiwan.
Beyond using the visit to try to keep “strategic stability” between the two countries, Trump seems to be pulling out all the diplomatic stops to show off for Xi. He has lavished praise on him as a “great leader” and described a warm relationship with the man he has called a friend. That's all while he's given Xi a pass on many issues.
Mississippi Sen. Roger Wicker, the Republican chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, criticized the “lavish welcome." He said during a speech on the Senate floor on Tuesday that Trump should not have invited the Chinese leader “based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party.”
Wicker archly suggested a list of topics that Trump could discuss with Xi at the state dinner, such as “the purposes of China’s massive military buildup, or about China’s clear support for Iran,” saying that “during every minute of dialogue” Trump should keep in mind that “his guest is a brutal, unelected and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose massive military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America.”
Trump has made it clear he wants to wow Xi, telling reporters in recent weeks that he was delighted his new “work of art” helicopter landing pad would be ready for the visit while bemoaning that his massive White House ballroom would not.
On Wednesday, Trump is expected to try to match the pageantry he was met with in China earlier this year. Xi wasn't there to meet Trump — he sent Chinese Vice President Han Zheng instead. But there was a long red carpet rolled out to meet Air Force One in Beijing. Along the sides were a military honor guard, a military band and about 300 Chinese youths waving Chinese and American flags and chanting, “Welcome, welcome! Warm welcome!” The children were wearing white and light blue uniforms that mirrored the traditional paint colors of the presidential plane.
Trump's airport ceremony will be followed on Thursday by more formalities, including an arrival ceremony at the White House and a review of troops. Before the black-tie dinner — which will feature tech industry leaders like Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and SpaceX’s Elon Musk — the two leaders are expected to dive into the weighty issues behind closed doors, even as expectations are low that the trip will produce any major breakthroughs in the relationship.
On Friday, Xi and Peng will be back at the White House for a private tea with the president and first lady Melania Trump before joining them on a tour of the National Archives in Washington. The White House has said they will view historic documents underscoring the relationship between the two countries.
Associated Press writer Mary Clare Jalonick contributed to this report.

AI trade outlook brightens on falling oil and Meta’s Muse agent ahead of Xi-Trump meeting
Nasdaq-100 hits record high while chip stocks in China and South Korea rebound, with investors betting that AI earnings can weather higher interest rates
The global AI trade is staging a comeback, as a confluence of falling oil prices, Meta Platforms’ launch of a new agentic tool, and anticipation surrounding the China-US leadership summit reignite interest in technology stocks.
The Nasdaq-100 Index hit an all-time high on Tuesday, surpassing the previous record set in June. In Asia, China’s chip-heavy Star Market 50 Index and South Korea’s Kospi gauge, which is heavily weighted towards memory chipmakers, have been bouncing back since July sell-offs.
The shift appears to mark a reversal in negative sentiment surrounding artificial intelligence stocks, which had been battered by inflationary fears and calls from some US tech companies to slow the development of new AI models due to safety concerns. Market sentiment pivoted as oil’s retreat below US$100 a barrel eased inflationary pressure and as Meta’s Muse agent reinforced demand across the AI supply chains.
Meanwhile, positive rhetoric from a preparatory trade talk before the sit-down between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump has fuelled optimism for a de-escalation of geopolitical tensions.

China’s racewalkers secured a landmark gold as they dominated the half marathons at the Asian Games on Wednesday, winning both the men’s and women’s events.
A new distance compared to the 20km version contested at previous Asian Games, Shi Shengji stormed to the men’s title at the Aichi-Nagoya race walking course in one hour, 23 minutes and 32 seconds.
The 19-year-old from Jiangsu built up a commanding lead of almost four and a half minutes over world and Asian double-record holder Toshikazu Yamanishi of Japan, who finished in 1:28:01.
Choe Byeong-kwong of South Korea took bronze in 1:28:35, while Hongkonger Chin Man-kit finished fifth out of nine contestants, crossing the line in 1:34:26. China’s Li Chenjie was disqualified.
