‘Dancing With the Stars’ Recap: Who Was Eliminated on Viral Hits Night?
- Week 2 of Dancing With the Stars Season 35 featured the contestants dancing to viral hits.
- The couples were dancing for scores from the judges and votes from viewers.
- At the end of the episode, the pair with the lowest combined scores and votes was eliminated.
Week 2 of Dancing With the Stars brought your favorite viral hits to the dance floor! During the two-part Season 35 premiere in Week 1, both new pros Adele Zaikman and Hailey Bills were eliminated with their celebs, Conner Leavitt and Sarah Jane Nader, respectively, but the show went on for the other 14 couples.
Throughout the September 22 episode, the celebs and their pro partners took the ballroom floor to wow the judges with dances to songs that have found popularity on social media, including “All the Things She Said” by Harrison, which went viral after being featured in Heated Rivalry, and “What Was I Made For?” by Billie Eilish, which had everyone in their feels after watching Barbie.
Scroll down for a complete recap of the episode.
Jenna Dewan & Val Chmerkovskiy — 21/30
After Carrie Ann Inaba‘s feedback last week about Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy’s teamwork, Dewan was determined to make a splash with a jive to “Animal” by KATSEYE. Bruno Tonioli raved, “What a way to start the show,” calling Dewan “a sexy beast [who] did not miss a beat.”
Inaba explained, “Tonight, what I saw was connected resistance.” She later added, “I’m excited because it was so good.” For Derek Hough‘s one-word response, he shared, “Fast-fierce-fantastic.” (We’re sure the hyphens were in there.)
View this post on Instagram
After their dance, Dewan told Julianne Hough that she really wanted to show Inaba how strong their partnership could be. With 7s from all three judges, Dewan finished with a 21/30.
Ciara Miller & Brandon Armstrong — 18/30
Last week, Ciara Miller got vulnerable on the dance floor, with Inaba declaring that she could “see” her. Ready to work on their frame, Miller and Brandon Armstrong took to the floor with a tango to “No Broke Boys” by Disco Lines and Tinashe.
While Miller’s heel got caught, Inaba cheered, “Ciara has entered the building!” According to Hough, the duo still needs to watch their frame, but he thought that Miller was absolutely radiant. During his one(ish) word statement, Tonioli shared, “Beautiful, my darling.”
View this post on Instagram
With 6s across the board, Miller got 18/30, exclaiming that she was incredibly grateful.
Tyler Cameron & Sharna Burgess — 16/30
Garrett Graham (Belmont Cameli), is that you? For their Week 2 dance, Bachelor Nation’s Tyler Cameron and pro Sharna Burgess danced a salsa to “Girls” by The Kid LAROI, which went viral after the song was featured on Off Campus. Trust us, Cameron’s moves were just as hot as the Briar U hockey star’s.
As Cameron and Burgess teased earlier in the week, his shirt did come off, and the Bachelor star did do the Off Campus fist-to-hips dance move. “You were lifting Sharna up like a He-Man sword,” Hough explained before calling out the content. “It felt more like a cabaret than a salsa.” Tonioli added, “I have to agree with Derek” after calling Cameron a “Terminator.” As Inaba briefly put it, “Agreed, but impressive”
View this post on Instagram
Dedicating their dance to the girls and the gays this week, Cameron received a 6 from Inaba and 5s from the guys, getting a 16/30.
Julia Stiles & Ezra Sosa — 16/30
According to actress Julia Stiles, she is reclaiming her relationship with being open and vulnerable in the public eye by being on Dancing With the Stars. She and Ezra Sosa took on the tango for Week 2 with “The Door” by Teddy Swims.
Tonioli told Stiles, “Some beats were very, very good but at times there were stumbles, and you know that.” Agreeing, Inaba shared, “What’s beautiful about you is your posture… But it’s also working against you.” Derek’s “one” word was “good performance.”
View this post on Instagram
With a 6 from Hough and 5s from Tonioli and Inaba, Stiles received a 16/30 from the judges.
Jackson Olson & Emma Slater — 18/30
After landing a collection of 5s last week, Jackson Olson is “determined” to do better. This week, Emma Slater challenged Olson to his first ballroom dance in frame, a foxtrot to “That’s So True” by Gracie Abrams.
Praised for a “smooth” foxtrot by Alfonso Ribeiro, Olson received rave reviews compared to last week. “Whoa, improvement,” Inaba told Olson. “You settled into it. The partnership is working.” Hough added, “I was really impressed by your frame,” explaining how important it is to maintain that form. For Tonioli’s one word, he told them, “What we all feel — charmed.”
View this post on Instagram
With 6s across the board, Slater was “ecstatic” to see a one-point bump from each judge. Olson received an 18/30.
Giada De Laurentiis & Alan Bersten — 12/30
After surprising everyone, including herself, Giada De Laurentiis hoped to surprise herself again with a salsa (and her first lifts) to “Bella Ciao” by Becky G. Both De Laurentiis and pro Alan Bersten appeared to have a tearful rehearsal process this week that Julianne Hough referred to as “healthy friction.”
Derek Hough pointed out a few missteps during their dance, sharing that De Laurentiis is still a little timid. As Tonioli put it, “You gave me salsa without spice, that is a problem.” He added, “You have to let it go. I can see you thinking.” Unfortunately, Inaba’s word for De Laurentiis was “Shake-y.”
View this post on Instagram
The full panel was booed as they gave 4s across the board. De Laurentiis received a 12/30, which she called “disappointing.”
Connor Wood & Rylee Arnold — 15/30
Content creator Connor Wood hoped to go viral with his tango with Rylee Arnold to “12 to 12” by Sombr. Telling Wood he was going to be brutally honest after the duo made a few noticeable mistakes during their dance, Tonioli explained, “There were a lot of mistakes tonight, and you know that… But the good bits were excellent.”
“That’s such a shame,” Inaba commented, giving multiple compliments before addressing their pitfall. “It’s a mistake, which is why our scores must be what they are.” For his one word, Hough shouted out Wood’s grandmother, with whom he went viral for the first time, saying, “Grandma Mimi.”
View this post on Instagram
Still, Wood received 5s across the board, with a 15/30.
Ezra Frech & Daniella Karagach — 21/30
After coming in third last week, Daniella Karagach challenged Ezra Frech to what she called the most difficult dance: The cha-cha. Together, they took the floor in shades to dance to “Low” by Flo Rida. “This ballroom was torn down tonight,” Ribiero exclaimed after their dance concluded.
“What the frick, Ezra Frech!” Inaba exclaimed, calling their dance “down and dirty,” before adding that the track star “demands excellence from himself.” Recalling his season with Paralympian Amy Purdy, Hough shared, “I am just in awe of you, my friend.”
View this post on Instagram
With 7s from all the judges, Frech received a 21/30.
Tatyana Ali & Jan Ravnik — 18/30
Preparing a foxtrot to “What Was I Made For?” by Billie Eilish with Jan Ravnik, Tatyana Ali looked back at overcoming harsh words from critics in her past. After a misstep through her off her game last week, Ali brought it for Week 2.
“You were absolutely beautiful,” Hough told Ali. “That was breathtaking.” Tonioli commented on the vulnerable dance sharing, “It had such a soft and gentle quality… Beautiful storytelling.” He joked, adding, “The footwork, I assume, was good, but it was lost in the fog.” Inaba’s one word was “touching.”
View this post on Instagram
Ali received 6s across the board, with an 18/30.
Amber Glenn & Pasha Pashkov — 21/30
Making an iconic reference to Heated Rivalry and her personal connection to the series having come out in 2019, Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov danced a tango to “All the Things She Said” by Harrison, who was in the ballroom DJing the song.

-《与星共舞》第35季第2周，参赛者随着热门歌曲跳舞。
-这对夫妇正在为评委的分数和观众的投票而跳舞。
-在这一集结束时，综合得分和选票最低的一对被淘汰。
《与星共舞》第二周将你最喜欢的热门歌曲带到了舞池！在第1周的第35季首播中，两位新职业选手阿黛尔·扎克曼和海莉·比尔分别与他们的名人康纳·莱维特和莎拉·简·纳德一起被淘汰，但该节目继续为其他14对夫妇播出。
在9月22日的整个节目中，这些名人和他们的职业伙伴在舞厅里用在社交媒体上流行的歌曲跳舞，让评委们惊叹不已，其中包括哈里森的《她说的一切》，在《激烈的竞争》中亮相后迅速走红，以及比利·艾利什的《我为什么而生？》，在看过芭比娃娃后，每个人都有同感。

‘Dancing With the Stars’ eliminates another couple during ‘Viral Hits Night’
“Dancing With the Stars” is continuing to whittle down the competition.
Celebrity chef and host Giada De Laurentiis and her pro partner, Alan Bersten, were eliminated at the end of the “Viral Hits Night” episode Tuesday night.
This week’s episode saw the Season 35 cast perform routines “inspired by some of the biggest viral hits and unforgettable moments that have taken the internet by storm,” per an ABC press release.
Prior to the elimination, co-hosts Julianne Hough and Alfonso Ribeiro revealed the other two couples in danger of going home: “Bachelor Nation” star Tyler Cameron (and partner Sharna Burgess) and “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” star Guillermo Rodriguez (and partner Witney Carson).
During Tuesday night’s episode, De Laurentiis landed at the bottom of the leaderboard with a score of 12/30 for their Salsa to Becky G’s “Bella Ciao.”
Three celebrities and their pros found themselves atop the scoreboard by scoring 21/30.
Those competitors included “Step Up” actress Jenna Dewan and partner Val Chmerkovskiy (who performed a Jive to KATSEYE’s “Animal”), Paralympian gold medalist Ezra French and partner Daniella Karagach (who performed a Cha Cha to Flo Rida’s “Low”) and Olympian gold medal-winning figure skater Amber Glenn and partner Pasha Pashkov (who performed a Tango to “All the Things She Said” by Harrison).
Stay one step ahead with all the exclusive tea on your favorite reality TV stars!
Sign up for Virtual Reali-Tea with Danny and Evan, our must-read newsletter!
Following closely behind was “Traitors” alum Maura Higgins and her partner, Mark Ballas, who scored a 19/30 for their Cha Cha to Earth, Wind & Fire’s “September.”
Four pairs also tied with a respectable score of 18/30, including “Summer House” star Ciara Miller and partner Brandon Armstrong (who performed a Tango to “No Broke Boys” by Disco Lines & Tinashe) as well as Savannah Bananas star Jackson Olson and partner Emma Slater (who performed a Foxtrot to “That’s So True” by Gracie Abrams).
Also scoring 18/30 were “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” star Tatyana Ali and partner Jan Ravnik (who performed a Foxtrot to Billie Eilish’s “What Was I Made For?”) and “Glee” alum Harry Shum Jr. and partner Jenna Johnson (who performed a Viennese Waltz to “Iris” by the Goo Goo Dolls).
Cameron and Burgess earned a 16/30 for their Salsa to “Girls” by The Kid LAROI, matching the score of “Save the Last Dance” actress Julia Stiles and pro partner Ezra Sosa’s Tango to “The Door.”
Comedian Connor Wood and pro partner Rylee Arnold’s Tango to “12 to 12” by sombr earned them a 15/30, while singer Taylor Hanson and pro partner Britt Stewart’s Cha Cha to DNCE’s “Cake By the Ocean” scored them a 15/30.
Landing at the bottom alongside De Laurentiis was Rodriguez and Carson’s Paso Doble to Rihanna’s “Where Have You Been,” which also scored them a 12/30.
Last week’s two-night premiere saw “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star Conner Leavitt and “Love Thy Nader” star Sarah Jane Nader sent packing in back-to-back eliminations.
On the flip side, Shum Jr. and Higgins topped the leaderboard in their respective nights — with the male celebrities performing in the first night of competition and the female celebrities hitting the ballroom during the second night.
New episodes of “DWTS” will air Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+, and will stream on Hulu the following day.

articles.title_orig: Trump Threatens Annihilation in Iran in UN Speech and Lays Out Winner-Takes-All Vision
articles.title_zh: Trump Threatens Annihilation in Iran in UN Speech and Lays Out Winner-Takes-All Vision
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump made multiple false claims in his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, though he largely stuck to a prepared text.
Here is a fact check of some of his assertions.
Trump, repeating a frequent false claim, said, “Since I took office, it has been my great honor to settle eight wars.”
He specified that he was talking about conflicts between Cambodia and Thailand; Kosovo and Serbia; Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo; India and Pakistan; Armenia and Azerbaijan; and the war in Gaza. And he has previously claimed that the other two wars he ended were last year’s brief conflict between Israel and Iran and a supposed war between Egypt and Ethiopia.
Trump’s “eight” figure is a clear exaggeration.
His list includes two situations that were never actually wars during his tenure. The situation between Egypt and Ethiopia was a diplomatic dispute over an Ethiopian dam project, not a war, and the mysterious supposed issue he says he resolved between Serbia and Kosovo was also not a war.
In addition, the war involving Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo has not ended despite a peace agreement brokered by the Trump administration. And though Trump cited the war in Gaza, Israel continues to conduct frequent attacks in the enclave despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement.
Trump did help to end the brief 2025 conflict between Israel and Iran, though Israel proceeded to join the US in starting another war against Iran in 2026.
Trump scoffed at dire warnings that artificial intelligence might eventually attack or kill people, claiming they are coming from “the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming, a name since reborn to climate change because the planet was cooling, not warming, and nobody was dead.”
There are at least four things wrong with his sentence about global warming.
First, the phrase “global warming” remains in widespread use even though the phrase “climate change” is also common; they mean different things. Climate scientists use both, often saying “global warming” when referring to the long-term trend of increasing global temperature and “climate change” when referring to the numerous effects the world is experiencing because of that trend. (NASA, part of the Trump-led federal government, explains the difference between the terms on its website.) For example, a 2023 report from the UN’s climate change panel is titled “Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report,” but it says this: “Human activities, principally through emissions of greenhouse gases, have unequivocally caused global warming, with global surface temperature reaching 1.1°C above 1850-1900 in 2011-2020.”
Second, while Trump didn’t say what time period he was talking about, he didn’t acknowledge that the world has continued to get warmer, not cooler. The UN’s World Meteorological Organization reported in January that “the past 11 years have been the 11 warmest on record,” with 2023, 2024 and 2025 the three very warmest — as NASA also found — though 2025 wasn’t as hot as 2024.
Third, experts widely disagree that “nobody” has died from the various impacts of a warming world. It’s impossible to pinpoint a precise death number, but some estimates total in the millions. The deaths are likely to continue; the World Health Organization says, “Between 2030 and 2050, climate change is expected to cause approximately 250,000 additional deaths per year, from undernutrition, malaria, diarrhea and heat stress alone.”
Fourth, while somebody somewhere might have said that “we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming,” that isn’t how an expert report framed the issue.
A widely discussed 2018 report from climate scientists said the world needed to sharply cut carbon emissions within the next 12 years to be on track to limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels; scientists said above that threshold, the potential deadly impacts from climate change would be larger. Though the 2018 report was often oversimplified by politicians, the expert claim was never that “we’ll all be dead in 12 years” — it was that significant action was needed within 12 years to improve the future. (The UN program reported earlier this month that the world is set to exceed the 1.5-degree increase, “likely within the next few years.”)
Trump delivered a more cautious version of his inaccurate previous boast that $21 trillion in investment is pouring into the US, this time saying, “We’ve secured commitments for $21 trillion in new investments from all over the planet.” His figure has no apparent basis even with the “secured commitments for” caveat; the White House has never been able to substantiate it.
When the president spoke at the UN, the White House’s own website claimed there had been “$11.2 trillion” in “major investment announcements” during Trump’s second term, far less than the “$21 trillion” in commitments the president cited. And a detailed CNN review in 2025 found the White House list was counting trillions in vague investment pledges, pledges that were about “bilateral trade” or “economic exchange” rather than investment in the US, and vague statements that didn’t even rise to the level of pledges.
The White House figure includes pledges from US-based companies as well as foreign entities. Federal data shows that new foreign direct investment in the US was about $232 billion in 2025.
Trump defended the Iran war at length. And he claimed, “The cowards and traitors would love to say the United States is low on munitions, but that’s not true. We have more munitions than we could ever possibly even think of using, and we’re building them at levels that we have never done before.”
We don’t have access to classified information on the precise current state of US munitions stockpiles, and it’s not clear who Trump is calling “cowards and traitors.” But it’s not just CNN and other media outlets that have reported that the war with Iran has depleted at least some US munitions levels; the federal inspector general overseeing the Defense Department and the nonpartisan federal Congressional Budget Office essentially said the same in separate reports released last week.
The inspector general report, which discussed the period from the beginning of April through the end of June, said a Defense Department acquisitions office “said that the munitions expenditure in (the war) has resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply.”
The report said the acquisitions office also noted that while the Pentagon “has begun to implement mitigation strategies, the defense industrial base requires ‘significant lead time’ to expand production capacities.” The report specified: “The most persistent bottlenecks remain in the production of solid rocket motors, the availability of high-grade explosives and propellants, and the recruitment of skilled manufacturing labor.”
The Congressional Budget Office report said there is a “shortfall” of missile defense interceptors and that the war will leave “the United States with a reduced inventory of interceptors for several years.” The report said the Defense Department had a “limited” inventory of interceptors even before Israel and the US attacked Iran during a brief conflict in June 2025, and that the budget office’s research indicates the US “has probably used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of those munitions since June 2025.”
“Given the number of missile defense interceptors that DoD has recently used, their currently low production rates, and the historical difficulty of scaling up their production, rebuilding DoD’s inventory of interceptors would probably take at least five years — even if production was increased,” the report said.
The Defense Department has consistently said it’s not true that there are any munitions shortfalls, and it did so again last week.

articles.title_orig: Ella Langley says 'Choosin' Texas' success is 'changing my life' after her song breaks Mariah Carey's record
articles.title_zh: Ella Langley says 'Choosin' Texas' success is 'changing my life' after her song breaks Mariah Carey's record
articles.content_orig:
Ella Langley knew "Choosin' Texas" was special. Even she couldn't have predicted just how far it would go.
On Tuesday night, Langley took to Instagram to celebrate making Billboard Hot 100 history this week when "Choosin' Texas" logged its 23rd week at No. 1, surpassing Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" for the longest reign at the top of the chart.
"I'm genuinely trying to find the words to explain what's going on in my brain today," Langley began her video. "What? I don't know. Thank you so much. Thank you for loving this song, for listening to it. I feel like… I just don't even know what to say at this point. I'm running out of hyperboles to describe how I feel, so I will just let my dog in the background show you his excitement," she continued as her dog barked.
"Just thank you. Thank you so much. It's changing my life. It's changing the lives of the writers of this song. It's changing the lives of my family and it is truly growing an atmosphere for something I'm gonna be able to do the rest of my life and I just… today doesn't feel like a real thing," Langley said. "It feels fake and somebody's going to come in and be like 'haha we're kidding the whole time just kidding.'"
ELLA LANGLEY SEEMINGLY FIRES BACK AFTER DOJA CAT'S BRUTAL TAKE ON HER CHART-TOPPING HIT
"I'm really excited to just experience a moment like this in my life," she said.
The country music star told her fans that she was going to celebrate tonight before ending with, "Choosin' T… that's the one huh?"
In a resurfaced interview with Billboard from March, when the song was still climbing, Langley admitted its success had already surpassed anything she imagined when she wrote it.
"When we wrote it, I knew it was going on the record. I honestly knew it was going to be the lead single," Langley told Billboard.
"And we love that song, but I don't think I could have ever imagined what's happening with it right now," she continued. "Like I said, every day I wake up and it's doing something that I didn't even know was a goal that I could have had."
"It's just nuts," Langley added. "It's crazy to see the ownership that the fans have taken over it. And the different demographics of people listening to the song is so cool."
What seemed unimaginable to Langley in March has since become historic.
ELLA LANGLEY'S 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' SPENDS 15 WEEKS AT NUMBER ONE ON THE BILLBOARD HOT 100
"Choosin' Texas" first entered the Hot 100 in November 2025, became Langley's first top 10 in January and reached No. 1 for the first time in February.
The song has also spent 41 weeks at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart.
Long before it became a record breaker, however, "Choosin' Texas" began with a story about a kangaroo.
Langley recalled writing the song during her first songwriting retreat with country superstar Miranda Lambert and two other writers.
"So, I was on a writer's retreat with Miranda," Langley explained in the resurfaced Billboard interview. "This is our first time that we had written together and obviously we were there with two others."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Billboard credits Langley, Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor as the four co-writers of "Choosin' Texas."
Langley said Lambert began telling her a story about a pet kangaroo.
"I learned at a young age she had a pet kangaroo and I wanted to ask her about it," Langley recalled. "So, I was like, 'Tell me about this kangaroo that you had. I need to know.'"
ELLA LANGLEY'S TEXAS PHOTO DUMP SENDS COUNTRY MUSIC FANS INTO A FRENZY ONLINE ON INSTAGRAM
Lambert told the group about once being pulled over with the kangaroo riding in the passenger seat and a dog in the back.
"She said she got pulled over and the kangaroo ended up getting her out of a ticket, but she's like, 'Of course, I had Texas plates on, too,'" Langley recalled.
ELLA LANGLEY JOINS MUSIC ROYALTY WITH 'INSANE' MILESTONE FOR 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS'
That was enough to spark the song.
"And I went, 'Well, she's from Texas, I can tell,'" Langley said. "And just from that phrase, it kind of all hit us."
According to Langley, the melody came almost immediately, with Lambert helping develop the story behind it.
"And 45 minutes later, we had that song written," Langley said. "And it was just, it was such a cool experience."
Lambert's involvement didn't end in the writing room.
Langley told Billboard that the country superstar was executive producing her next record and had become someone she could turn to for advice.
"There's not a rulebook to this job," Langley said. "So to be able to have someone like her to ask questions and think, you know, is it, should I be doing this? She's like, 'Hell yeah, you should be doing this.'"
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Even Lambert was surprised by what was happening with "Choosin' Texas."
"My team's calling me every day freaking out about this song," Langley recalled Lambert telling her.
At the time of the March interview, the song had reached No. 5 on the Hot 100.
"How crazy is that?" Langley said.
"And for me, like, what, me? You mean me?"
Six months later, "Choosin' Texas" stands alone as the longest-running No. 1 song in Hot 100 history.
Langley's historic week comes as she continues performing across the country.

The singer recently shared photos from stops in Oxford, Mississippi; Athens, Georgia; and Jacksonville, Florida.
"Oxford, Athens & Jacksonville ❤️," she captioned the Instagram post.
The images showed Langley performing with her guitar, posing near an Ole Miss sign in a dress and red boots, holding a snake and preparing backstage in front of a lighted mirror. Another captured an older couple dancing during her show.
Fans celebrated her record in the comments.
"Congrats @ellalangleymusic on passing Mariah!" one person wrote.

articles.title_orig: Trump backs ban on diesel exports
articles.title_zh: 特朗普支持禁止柴油出口
articles.summary_zh: 特朗普称支持禁止柴油出口，美国柴油均价已飙升至每加仑6.52美元的创纪录水平，同比上涨77%。
articles.content_orig:
President Trump said Tuesday that he would support banning exports of diesel fuel.
"I've said let's not send out the diesel," the president said on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. "We make a lot of diesel. It could have a little bit of an effect on regular automobile gasoline because when you do that, you know, it's a sort of a flow. It's a balance."
Trump added, "But no, I've called for it. I've called for it within my people. I've been talking about it."
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he's examining whether a diesel export ban is feasible, given overall refining capacity and whether a full or partial ban would work.
The national average price of diesel fuel has surged to an all-time record of $6.52 per gallon, according to AAA, a staggering 77% increase compared to this time last year.
Driven primarily by global supply crunches from the wars in Iran and Ukraine, the sudden spike is acting as a massive tax on the US supply chain, which is heavily reliant on diesel to move goods. Because diesel is the economy's primary industrial fuel, its high cost is spilling over into consumer prices nationwide.
Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis for GasBuddy, posted on X, "this will backfire and is not good."
"U.S. diesel prices are determined not by a U.S. supply and demand balance, but a global one," De Haan wrote. "Keeping distillates and diesel [at] home does not change the world price that reference our prices. You can't fence off a globally traded commodity by executive order and expect the global price to stop applying to it."
Economist Joseph Brusuelas warned that the export ban could backfire for another reason: if energy producers pull back on production. The US produces 5.3 million barrels per day, above the 3.6 million barrels of daily domestic demand. He says an export ban would create a short-term domestic surplus, which would then have to be sold at a discount. That, in turn, could cause energy firms to pull back on production, sending prices back up.
Jennifer Schonberger is a veteran financial journalist covering markets, the economy, and investing. At Yahoo Finance, she covers the Federal Reserve, Congress, the White House, the Treasury, the SEC, the economy, cryptocurrencies, and the intersection of Washington policy with finance. Follow her on X @Jenniferisms and on Instagram.

articles.content_zh:
特朗普总统周二表示，他将支持禁止柴油燃料出口。
“我说过，别把柴油送出去。”总统在联合国大会场边说。“我们生产大量柴油。这可能会对普通汽车汽油产生一点影响，因为你知道，这是一种流动，是一种平衡。”
特朗普补充说：“不过，是的，我已经呼吁过。我在自己人中间呼吁过。我一直在谈这件事。”
财政部长斯科特·贝森特表示，他正在研究柴油出口禁令是否可行，包括整体炼油产能，以及全面还是部分禁令有效。
据AAA数据，美国柴油平均价格已飙升至每加仑6.52美元的史上最高纪录，与去年同期相比惊人地上涨了77%。
主要由伊朗和乌克兰战争造成的全球供应紧张推动，这一突然飙升正对美国供应链造成沉重打击——美国供应链严重依赖柴油运输货物。由于柴油是经济的主要工业燃料，其高成本正在向全国消费者价格蔓延。
GasBuddy石油分析主管帕特里克·德哈恩在X上发文称，“这会适得其反，并不好”。
“美国柴油价格不是由美国的供需平衡决定的，而是由全球供需决定的。”德哈恩写道。“把馏分油和柴油留在国内并不会改变决定我们价格的全球价格。你不能用行政命令围住一种全球交易的商品，却指望全球价格不再适用于它。”
经济学家约瑟夫·布鲁苏拉斯警告说，出口禁令可能因另一个原因适得其反：如果能源生产商缩减产量。美国日产量530万桶，高于360万桶的国内日需求量。他说，出口禁令会造成短期国内过剩，届时必须折价出售。这反过来可能导致能源公司缩减产量，推高价格。

Editor’s Note: After publication of this story, the official X account of CASI shared a statement “that Air University has decided to close the China Aerospace Studies Institute,” despite the Air Force’s previous statement on the status of the organization. Breaking Defense has requested clarification from the service and will update this story with more information.
WASHINGTON — The Air Force is eliminating civilian staff roles for a service-run organization dedicated to studying Chinese airpower, but is not closing shop on the research entity, according to an Air Force spokesperson.
In a statement to Breaking Defense, the spokesperson said that in response to “an ongoing civilian restructure within” the Air Force’s Air Education and Training Command, civilian staff “will no longer be assigned to China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI).” The spokesperson added that CASI’s “mission continues” and will be executed by “leveraging assigned military service members to accomplish its objectives.”
Affected civilian employees “will continue in their current positions until further notice and will be evaluated for reassignment,” the spokesperson said.
CASI is a premiere, government-run think tank that regularly publishes research on Beijing’s air and space forces. The entity shares its findings within the US military and the broader defense community to promote understanding of China’s military prowess, with the goal of shaping policy and strategy.
The organization’s most recent work was published Monday. The paper, entitled From Vision to Vigilance: How Beijing’s Space-Science Roadmap Builds a Real-Time Kill Webb, explores how technologies ostensibly geared toward space exploration could instead “support persistent, multi-spectral coverage across the Pacific with near-real time refresh,” the paper’s introduction reads. Those technologies could then be used for military purposes to aid what defense officials call a “kill web,” essentially a network of integrated sensors that can provide multiple ways to track and strike a target.
Trouble at CASI first surfaced on Monday when a civilian staffer posted online about roles being eliminated, including a claim that the Air Force planned to “shutter” the institute. The move, coming the week that Chinese President Xi Jinping is slated to visit the United States, prompted questions about similar study projects run by the Army and Navy.

articles.summary_zh: 中国发射首颗商用无线电跟踪卫星实现电子战飞跃
articles.content_orig:
China launches its first commercial radio-tracking satellites in electronic warfare leap
The trio of satellites, named after an all-hearing mythical beast, can track enemy warships, hidden radars and electronic jammers
China has just taken a quiet but critical step in space-based electronic warfare.
A Lijian-1 Y18 rocket lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northern China at noon on Sunday, carrying nine satellites. Among them were three Diting-01 satellites, which successfully entered their planned orbit.
The trio is named after Diting, a beast from Chinese mythology that crouches beneath the desk of Ksitigarbha, the bodhisattva of the underworld, and can identify all things simply by listening.
The name perfectly captures what these satellites are designed to do.
articles.content_zh:
中国发射首颗商用无线电跟踪卫星实现电子战飞跃
这三颗卫星以一种全听力神话中的野兽命名，可以追踪敌方军舰、隐藏雷达和电子干扰器
中国刚刚在天基电子战方面迈出了一个安静但关键的一步。
周日中午，一枚李剑一号Y18火箭从中国北方酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空，携带9颗卫星。其中包括三颗Diting-01卫星，它们成功进入了计划轨道。
这三人组以中国神话中的野兽地丁命名，地丁蹲在地藏菩萨的桌子下，只需倾听就能识别一切。
这个名字完美地捕捉到了这些卫星的设计目的。

articles.content_orig:
Sea turtle makes rare, first-ever nest on West Coast beach thanks to warm waters from looming 'Super' El Niño
Due to the powerful El Niño, water temperatures are way above normal, which is bringing rare sea life to the shores of California.
- A sea turtle made the first-ever recorded natural nesting on the West Coast.
- The olive ridley sea turtle burrowed a nest near Seal Beach in California.
- Another sea turtle burrowed a nest on a beach a few miles away.
ORANGE COUNTY, Calif. – A rare moment along the beach in Orange County, California, captured an Olive Ridley sea turtle digging a nest and laying eggs.
According to NOAA, this is the first-ever recorded natural nesting for any sea turtle species on the West Coast.
WHERE DO ANIMALS GO WHEN FALL ARRIVES? INSIDE THE INCREDIBLE MIGRATIONS HAPPENING ACROSS THE US
"These sea turtles are found worldwide, primarily in the tropical waters of the Pacific, Indian, and Atlantic oceans. Major Pacific nesting populations span Mexico, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Panama," said the NOAA. "While occasionally seen in Southern California following warm currents, this species has never been documented to nest in the United States."
Video shared by NOAA Fisheries shows the turtle digging and burying its eggs in the sand, paying no mind to the observer behind it.

Additionally, three days later, officials observed another sea turtle on a beach a few miles away near Huntington Beach. Still, it is currently unclear if this is the same turtle as before.
These adult sea turtles can weigh up to 100 pounds and can live an estimated 30-50 years.
With nesting season coming to an end, forecasters point to the brewing ‘Super’ El Niño as the reason for this rare event.
Due to the powerful El Niño, water temperatures are way above normal, which is bringing rare sea life to the shores of California.

Thankfully, officials will monitor the testing area, keeping it fenced and protected over the next 45-60 days as they wait for the cute baby turtles to hatch.
The best thing to do while a sea turtle is digging a nest is to give the animal plenty of distance and not disturb the fencing protecting it.

美国国家海洋和大气管理局渔业部分享的视频显示，这只海龟在沙子里挖洞埋蛋，根本不理会身后的观察者。在阿拉斯加国家公园，与竞争2026年肥熊周冠军的熊们见面此外，三天后，官员们在亨廷顿海滩附近几英里外的海滩上观察到另一只海龟。尽管如此，目前尚不清楚这是不是和以前一样的乌龟。

articles.title_orig: Trump berates CNN’s Kaitlan Collins after ban: ‘You shouldn’t be covering me’
articles.title_zh: 特朗普在禁令后斥责CNN的凯特兰·柯林斯：“你不应该报道我”
articles.summary_zh: 白宫媒体禁令后，特朗普在联合国与美国有线电视新闻网的凯特兰·柯林斯进行了紧张的交流：“你不应该在这里”
articles.content_orig:
CNN’s Kaitlan Collins’ 7-Word Answer to Donald Trump’s Question Goes Viral
Kaitlan Collins didn't back down when Donald Trump challenged her right to report outside the United Nations on Tuesday. The CNN chief White House correspondent fired back with a seven-word reply that went viral. This turned a press moment into another flashpoint between the president and the network he is trying to shut out of official coverage.
Donald Trump questions Kaitlan Collins during UN visit
The president traveled to New York City to address the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. As he approached the UN entrance, Kaitlan Collins called out a question drawn from new CNN polling: "Two-thirds of Americans don't think the U.S. is winning the war with Iran. When will it end?"
Donald Trump stopped and questioned why the network had sent her at all. "I'm surprised that CNN is here covering me. You shouldn't be here!" he said. Collins answered: "The United Nations allowed us in, sir." The president pressed on, telling her, "You should not be here covering me. You said you weren't going to cover me. You shouldn't be covering me." He then left the press scrum without answering her question about Iran.
Trump: "I'm surprised CNN is here is covering me. You shouldn't be here."
CNN's Kaitlan Collins: "The United Nations allowed us in, sir." pic.twitter.com/fMrWCnABEO
— philip lewis (@Phil_Lewis_) September 22, 2026
The UN visit came days after Donald Trump announced on September 18 that he was banning CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House "effective immediately," repeating his long-standing claim that they publish "fake news." Staffers from all three outlets lost their press badges on Saturday.
On Monday, the three organizations sued Trump and three White House officials, arguing the ban violates the First Amendment and "brazenly discriminates based on editorial viewpoint." The same day, ABC News, CBS News, NBC News, and Fox News, which share White House TV pool duties with CNN, suspended their own coverage of White House events to protest the ban.
For now, Collins' calm seven-word reply stands as the most-shared moment from a UN visit already steeped in press-freedom controversy.
The post CNN's Kaitlan Collins' 7-Word Answer to Donald Trump's Question Goes Viral appeared first on Reality Tea.
articles.content_zh:
白宫媒体禁令后，特朗普在联合国与美国有线电视新闻网的凯特兰·柯林斯进行了紧张的交流：“你不应该在这里”
在您的搜索结果中查看更多我们的报道。
在谷歌上添加《纽约邮报》
在全球舞台上进行高风险外交的一天，唐纳德·特朗普总统在访问联合国时对一位著名的美国记者说：“你不应该来这里。”
“很荣幸来到这里，”特朗普周二在联合国大会演讲前走进联合国大门时说，他面对的是美国有线电视新闻网的凯特兰·柯林斯，他经常成为他的愤怒目标。“我很惊讶CNN在这里报道我。你不应该在这里报道。你说过你不会报道我的。”
正如柯林斯后来在节目中指出的那样，美国有线电视新闻网没有说任何类似的话。几天前，政府禁止美国有线电视新闻网与NOW和Politico一起进入白宫，并取消了该网络的共享税。但美国有线电视新闻网已被联合国接纳为定期认证的媒体。
无论如何，这一紧张时刻清楚地提醒人们，特朗普与他反对其报道为“假新闻”的新闻机构之间的激烈冲突在短短几天内就急剧升级。
目前的禁令是这三家媒体周一提起的联合诉讼的主题，要求法官认定政府的举动违宪。白宫必须在周二之前作出回应，听证会定于周三下午举行。
特朗普表示，他有权“清除假新闻”
周二晚些时候，特朗普进一步强化了他的言论，并表示负面报道对国家来说是危险的。
当被问及如果法院做出不利于白宫的裁决，他是否会允许媒体重返白宫时，他说：“好吧，很可能会，因为这位法官不是一位特别公平的法官。”他指的是美国地区法官蒂莫西·凯利，他在2017年任命了他，并在2018年的一个类似案件中下令恢复CNN记者的访问权限。
“所以你永远不知道，”特朗普补充道。“我认为我们有权清除假新闻。”
特朗普的评论呼应了他自周五宣布禁令以来所做的其他评论。他提到了“故意负面报道”，但没有引用具体的报道——只是笼统地说是“假新闻”——作为禁令的理由。
这项禁令和诉讼是总统（尤其是在他的第二任期内）与他认为不利的媒体之间长期冲突的一部分。特朗普在法庭上做出了回应，或者采取了监管行动。他还亲自或多次抨击个别记者

articles.title_orig: E.U. drops sanctions on two of Russia’s richest oligarchs despite Kyiv’s outcry
articles.title_zh: E.U. drops sanctions on two of Russia’s richest oligarchs despite Kyiv’s outcry
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine anger as EU removes Russian oligarchs from sanctions list
The European Union is to remove sanctions on two oligarchs imposed after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, according to reports, prompting anger in Ukraine.
France had campaigned for Russian-Uzbek billionaire Alisher Usmanov to be taken off the list, citing "national security concerns". Luxembourg called for the removal of Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman, who is suing the country for the release of frozen assets.
Latvia initially opposed the deal but agreed to a compromise, part of which involved extending sanctions on nearly 3,000 other individuals and entities for three years.
Ukrainian officials said the move was "unacceptable" and sent the wrong signal to Moscow.
"Moscow is celebrating because it got what it wanted: a sense of impunity, the humiliation of the EU, and division among Europeans," Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said on X.
He urged all EU member states to instead announce national sanctions on the two individuals. Latvia has already said it would do so.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov earlier welcomed the prospect of the two oligarchs being taken off the list, claiming the EU's sanctions were illegal and all Russians should be removed.
Usmanov founded USM Holding company, an investment group that owns iron, steel and copper suppliers, and the Megafon telecommunications company. He has in the past had ties with the English Premier League clubs Arsenal and Everton.
The EU froze his assets in 2022, describing him as "a pro-Kremlin oligarch with particularly close ties to Russian president Vladimir Putin". Usmanov said the decision was "unfair".
It has been reported that France's initiative was linked to a prospective prisoner release deal with Azerbaijan.
Fridman, a Russian-Israeli citizen born in Ukraine, is the founder of the Alfa Group investment conglomerate, with key interests in energy and banking. The EU has described him as a top Russian financier and enabler of Putin's inner circle.
Fridman himself said at the time of Russia's full-scale invasion that the conflict should end as soon as possible, but avoided outright condemnation of President Putin.
His Russian-Latvian business partner Pyotr Aven was stripped of Latvia's highest civilian honour in 2022 for failing to condemn the invasion of Ukraine.
This may have influenced Latvia's opposition to the move, vetoing it in a vote by EU ambassadors on Monday.
However, on Tuesday it changed its vote to an abstention as a compromise was reached. The new deal involved extending sanctions on some remaining 2,600 individuals and entities to three years. Until now, sanctions had to be renewed every six months.
Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs also announced that France had agreed to start talks with Latvia about joining a French nuclear deterrence initiative and strengthen its military presence in Latvia.

articles.title_orig: Oil falls after U.S. and Iran talk for hours at UN meeting
articles.title_zh: Oil falls after U.S. and Iran talk for hours at UN meeting
articles.content_orig:
Oil fell Wednesday, amid optimism that supply disruptions would ease following U.S.-Iran talks, which raised hopes of a diplomatic solution to the conflict in the Middle East.
Futures for international benchmark Brent crude for November delivery dropped 0.89% to $98.37 a barrel as of 1:12 a.m. ET. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for November fell 1.5% to $89.16 per barrel.
President Donald Trump said Tuesday that U.S. officials had a "very good meeting" with Iran's delegation and that it lasted about three hours. Earlier in his address to the U.N., Trump said he has a "big decision" over whether to reach a deal with Tehran or "annihilate" the country.
Reuters reported on Tuesday that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the U.S. agrees to ease military pressure and lift its blockade of Iranian ports.
"Pakistan's mediation efforts with Tehran could also reduce the risk of a broader escalation," said Paolo Broccardo, chief executive officer at private digital bank BankPro.
Oil prices are also unlikely to see a huge jump for now, he said.
"Over the past five consecutive sessions, the price has fallen by almost 12%, retreating once again from the 'intervention zone' above $100, where we have repeatedly seen intensified peace-building efforts from both sides," Broccardo said.

articles.title_orig: Texas Rangers accuse Camp Mystic of criminal offenses in children’s deaths
articles.title_zh: 得克萨斯游骑兵队指控神秘营地在儿童死亡事件中犯有刑事罪
articles.summary_zh: 法庭文件显示，去年德克萨斯州发生毁灭性洪水，27名女孩死亡，神秘营地面临刑事调查，其中可能包括过失杀人或过失杀人指控。
articles.content_orig:
Camp Mystic faces a criminal investigation that could include manslaughter or negligent homicide charges in the deaths of 27 girls amid devastating flooding in Texas last year, court documents show.
In applications for search warrants executed last week, investigators sought to obtain the electronic communications of the camp’s owners, saying they could provide evidence of manslaughter, negligent homicide, child abandonment or other crimes. No charges have been brought, and a representative of the camp did not immediately return messages seeking comment.
Brant Johnston, with the Texas Rangers, wrote in an affidavit that Camp Mystic had inadequate emergency plans, failed to conduct emergency drills or training, and in some cabins did not have enough adult counselors. Its owners neglected to take precautions by relocating children from low-lying cabins despite having monitored late-night flood warnings, Johnston wrote.
“Young campers cannot reasonably be expected to independently recognize a rapidly developing, life-threatening hazard or to organize and execute an evacuation absent direction from an adequate number of adult supervisors,” Johnston wrote.
He concluded: “Camp Mystic, LLC was aware of and consciously disregarded a substantial and unjustifiable risk of death to the campers in their care.”
Twenty-five campers and two teenage counselors at the Christian all-girls camp were killed as the raging Guadalupe River surged beyond its banks before dawn on July 4, 2025. Camp Mystic owner Richard Eastland also died in the flood.
For decades, Camp Mystic was a summer staple and an institution for generations of families, who dropped off their girls at the sleepaway camp to ride horses, canoe, fish and attend Bible studies. The camp did not reopen this year, and it has filed for bankruptcy reorganization.
All told, the destructive flooding killed at least 136 people along a several-mile stretch of the river, raising questions about how things went so terribly wrong.
Attorneys for some of the victims’ families welcomed the search warrants but said they should not have been necessary.
“For more than a year, families of the 27 angels killed at Camp Mystic have fought, begged, and pleaded with the Eastland family for accountability and answers,” Christina Yarnell and Brad Beckworth, attorneys for the family of victim Cile Steward, said in a written statement. “Instead, the Eastlands have held hostage the information and answers owed to parents who deserve, more than anyone, to know the details surrounding their daughters’ final moments.”
Steward’s body still has not been found.
Johnston wrote in the warrant that he made several visits to Camp Mystic and that he and other investigators have conducted interviews with witnesses, flood victims and people associated with the camp. But several people, including members of the Eastland family and other top camp officials, refused interviews, Johnston wrote.
The Eastland family and other camp leaders have testified in courtrooms and in front of the state Legislature in the months since the flood, however, with camp director Edward Eastland offering a tearful apology.
articles.content_zh:
法庭文件显示，去年德克萨斯州发生毁灭性洪水，27名女孩死亡，神秘营地面临刑事调查，其中可能包括过失杀人或过失杀人指控。
在上周执行的搜查令申请中，调查人员试图获得营地主人的电子通信，称他们可以提供过失杀人、过失杀人、遗弃儿童或其他犯罪的证据。没有提出任何指控，营地的一名代表也没有立即回复寻求置评的消息。
得克萨斯游骑兵队的布兰特·约翰斯顿在一份宣誓书中写道，神秘营地的应急计划不足，未能进行应急演习或培训，一些小屋没有足够的成人辅导员。约翰斯顿写道，尽管监测了深夜的洪水警报，但它的主人忽视了采取预防措施，将儿童从低洼的小屋中转移出来。
约翰斯顿写道：“在没有足够数量的成年主管的指导下，不能合理地期望年轻的露营者独立识别迅速发展、危及生命的危险，或组织和执行疏散。”。他总结道：“神秘营地有限责任公司意识到并有意识地忽视了他们所照顾的露营者面临的实质性和不合理的死亡风险。”
2025年7月4日黎明前，肆虐的瓜达卢佩河在岸边汹涌而过，基督教全女子营地的25名露营者和两名青少年辅导员被杀。神秘营地的主人理查德·伊斯特兰也在洪水中丧生。
几十年来，神秘营地一直是夏季的主食，也是几代家庭的机构，他们把女儿送到过夜营地骑马、划独木舟、钓鱼和参加圣经学习。该营地今年没有重新开放，并已申请破产重组。总而言之，这场破坏性的洪水在几英里长的河流沿岸造成至少136人死亡，这引发了人们对事情是如何变得如此糟糕的质疑。
一些受害者家属的律师对搜查令表示欢迎，但表示没有必要。
受害者Cile Steward家人的律师Christina Yarnell和Brad Beckworth在一份书面声明中表示：“一年多以来，在神秘营地遇害的27名天使的家人一直在与Eastland家人斗争、恳求和恳求，要求他们承担责任和回答。”。相反，东地大学将欠父母的信息和答案扣为人质，而父母理应得到更多

articles.title_orig: Trump Cites National Security as He Faces Pushback on Press Ban, D.C. Arch and More
articles.title_zh: Trump Cites National Security as He Faces Pushback on Press Ban, D.C. Arch and More
articles.content_orig:
Trump's D.C. arch is now a military complex. Here's how that complicates things
President Trump's weekend announcement that his proposed D.C. arch will double as a "top grade Military Complex" has raised even more questions about the controversial structure — and the already-fraught approval process.
Trump wrote Sunday on Truth Social that the 250-foot structure will "house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas," in addition to storing ammunition.
It's a far cry from the administration's original vision for the arch, which Trump first unveiled last October.
At the time, he told journalists it was being built to honor "me." The administration has since characterized it as a tribute to the United States' 250th anniversary and a tourist attraction.
"The Triumphal Arch in Memorial Circle is going to be one of the most iconic landmarks not only in Washington, D.C., but throughout the world," the White House has repeatedly told NPR, as recently as Tuesday.
National Park Service renderings and presentations touted an observation deck with views of Arlington National Cemetery and the National Mall, potentially including a cafe and gift shop. Those were approved by the Trump-packed Commission of Fine Arts in May.
But the word "military" did not surface until earlier this month, when Interior Secretary Doug Burgum announced on social media that excavation work would soon begin at the "Great Triumphal Arch and Military Observation Deck."
That announcement drew immediate pushback — and a judge's intervention — because it still needs a final green light from the National Capital Planning Commission. That cannot happen until other federally required historic preservation reviews are completed.
Historic preservation advocates have long said that the process was moving too quickly, and are now struggling with what to make of Trump's abrupt about-face.
"So suddenly, to take a resource that was not about security at all … and now turn that on its head, it seems to me we're back to square one because we're reviewing a different facility than when this started," said Charles Birnbaum, CEO and founding president of the Cultural Landscape Foundation, one of the outside groups involved in the historic preservation review.
As part of that process, the National Park Service last week asked preservation groups to provide feedback by Monday on its proposed "Memorandum of Agreement" (MOA) to move forward with the arch. Birnbaum told the agency over email — and reiterated to NPR — that "we view this MOA as DOA [dead on arrival]."
Birnbaum called the process "whiplash-inducing." He said the next steps are unclear, especially since a fortified military site would presumably require additional measures, from fencing to security, that have not come before federal panels yet.
The White House, Interior Department and National Park Service did not respond to NPR's questions about plans to submit new proposals for review. The Federal Aviation Administration also referred questions to the White House.
The FAA had just released findings on Friday of a monthslong evaluation, concluding that the arch — which would stand directly in the approach path into D.C.'s main airport — would not pose a risk to airspace. But that review did not take into account the presence of military drones, as noted by U.S. Rep. Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat.
"Putting a drone launching site directly in the landing path for DCA is a stupid, dangerous, and unworkable idea," Beyer said in a statement Tuesday. "But if Trump wants to pursue it, the FAA's prior work over the past six months to rubber stamp this proposal with a dubious safety study will be obsolete, and they will have to do it all over again."
Will the national security argument work for Trump again?
The arch was already facing legal questions, including about its compliance with D.C. building height limits.
It's also the subject of an ongoing lawsuit: A group including three Vietnam War veterans sued earlier this year over its lack of Congressional approval. The administration has not sought it, citing a 1925 law that allowed for the construction of a pair of 166-foot columns at that location that were ultimately never built.
The lawyer representing the veterans, Nicolas Sansone of Public Citizen Litigation Group, said in a statement Sunday that "the President's new justification for this wildly unpopular construction does nothing to cure its fundamental illegality."
Trump said in his post that he agreed to convert the arch into a military complex "at the strong request of the United States Military, and for national security purposes." A Pentagon spokesperson told NPR it had nothing to add beyond Trump's post.
Harold Hongju Koh, a former State Department legal advisor who now teaches international law at Yale Law School, called Trump's justification "laughable and pretextual."
"If there are dangers to which you need to have drones and snipers … Why don't you just move them there now? Why do you need to build an arch?" Koh asked. "Secondly, if the arch is what's creating the national security problem, so much that you need to have these mobile protections on board, then just don't build the arch."
Koh said that if Trump is truly concerned about a threat on the National Mall, he should hold a classified briefing to that effect and ask Congress to militarize the existing monuments. But he thinks it's more likely that Trump is playing the national security card in the hopes of boosting his case in court.
"It's the lipstick he puts on every pig," Koh said. "Immigration is for national security. Terrorists are for national security. Building a border wall is for national security. Building a ballroom is for national security."
The Trump administration has argued that construction of its White House ballroom must continue for national security purposes, citing the military complex it plans to build underneath. The Supreme Court allowed construction to continue in a ruling earlier this month, citing issues of plaintiffs' standing rather than the project's underlying legality.
But experts are skeptical that a national security argument can be made for the arch, especially since the structure would stand a stone's throw from both the Pentagon and Joint Base Myer-Henderson Hall.
"The difference is that the bunker reflects a widely accepted need to protect the president. It's bipartisan," said Mark Cancian, a retired Marine Corps colonel and military expert at the Center for Strategic International Studies. "There doesn't seem to be any need — there certainly hasn't been any need articulated beforehand — about why this facility would need drones and snipers."
Koh and others interviewed by NPR believe the administration is rushing to start construction before the November midterm elections, which could shift the makeup of Congress and potentially bring the arch to a halt.
On Tuesday, a group of lawmakers — five Democrats and one Independent — wrote a letter to Burgum demanding that the administration stop work on the arch. They questioned its legality and cited the Trump administration's own findings about its negative impacts on Arlington National Cemetery and other nearby historic sites.
"Putting the President's ego ahead of these memorials adds another stain on this administration's legacy," they wrote.

articles.content_orig:
Gable Steveson issues statement on UFC 331 loss, 2019 sexual assault arrest
Gable Steveson has broken his silence three days after UFC 331.
Steveson (4-1 MMA, 1-1 UFC) was viciously knocked out by Sean Sharaf (5-2 MMA, 1-2 UFC) in just 12 seconds Saturday in Los Angeles, marking the first MMA defeat for the Olympic gold medalist. It was a shocking moment as he became the biggest betting favorite ever to lose a UFC fight, and it was only a small piece of what many considered a disastrous PR week for him.
Prior to the fight, Sharaf went personal at the pre-fight press conference when he brought up Steveson's 2019 arrest for sexual assault. He called him "The Loophole," which is a non-affectionate nickname online fans have placed on Steveson after the prosecutor of the case alluded to how a loophole in the law may have contributed to his innocence.
Moreover, Steveson was relentlessly booed by fans at the press conference, ceremonial weigh-ins, on his walk to the octagon and his controversial exit following the crushing defeat.
It took several days after the fight, but on Tuesday, Steveson shared a lengthy statement on social media with his perspective on his checkered past, as well as addressing what went wrong inside the octagon at UFC 331.
Check out the full statement below (via Instagram):
This statement is for my family, my friends, my fans, and the people who truly know me and know the kind of man I am. I know there are people who will never support me, no matter what I say or do. that's their choice. But I'm speaking to the people who know me not just as an athlete, but as a husband and a father to a young daughter.
Prior to and during fight week, an incident from my college years was brought up by my opponent. I believe it was raised to get in my head, but it also reopened something that had been addressed years ago.
I want to be clear: I did not do anything alleged. I was never charged with a crime, and the matter was ultimately dropped by the district attorney. The allegations were not ignored nor brushed aside. They were thoroughly and heavily reviewed as I fully cooperated with law enforcement, including a separate Title IX review.
There were no criminal charges, no conviction, and no finding of responsibility against me.The matter was closed, and there is no pending legal issue involving me. my own attorney did their own investigation and stated on the record that even if the law was changed, I would have the same outcome, which now speaks for itself.
I understand how serious allegations like this are, and I understand that people may have questions when they hear only part of a story. Moving forward, I am going to keep focusing on my wife, my daughter, my family, and the work in front of me. To the people who support me, thank you. I know who I am. my family knows who I am. The people who have walked with me through life know who I am. That's what matters to me, and that's where I'm going to keep my focus.
As for my opponent, congratulations, you caught me. A mistake on my end was made. It was your night. Just like my wrestling days after my loss, I came back with an undeniable will to win and focus that led me to the top of my sport. The result of Saturday night, I believe, will catapult me to do the same. I will be great, and this won't deny me.
Steveson, 26, did not give a timeline for his planned return to the octagon, or what he expects for himself next.
Many questioned whether this defeat would deter him from continuing an MMA career, but it appears Steveson is determined to push forward and overcome a significant setback.
articles.content_zh:
Gable Steveson就UFC 331失利、2019年性侵被捕发表声明盖布尔·史蒂文森在UFC 331赛后三天打破了沉默。
周六在洛杉矶，史蒂夫森（4-1 MMA，1-1 UFC）在短短12秒内被肖恩·沙拉夫（5-2 MMA，1-2 UFC）恶意淘汰，这是这位奥运金牌得主在综合格斗比赛中的首次失利。这是一个令人震惊的时刻，因为他成为有史以来最受欢迎的输掉UFC比赛的人，而这只是许多人认为对他来说是灾难性公关周的一小部分。
在战斗之前，Sharaf在战前新闻发布会上谈到了Steveson 2019年因性侵被捕的情况。他称他为“漏洞”，这是在案件检察官暗示法律漏洞可能导致他无罪后，粉丝们在网上给史蒂维森起的一个非深情的绰号。
此外，史蒂维森在新闻发布会、正式称重、走向八角形以及在惨败后有争议的退出时，都遭到了球迷的无情嘘声。比赛结束几天后，史蒂维森在社交媒体上分享了一份长篇声明，阐述了他对自己曲折过去的看法，并解决了UFC 331八角形内部的问题。查看下面的完整声明（通过Instagram）：
这句话是写给我的家人、朋友、粉丝，以及那些真正了解我、知道我是什么样的人的。我知道有些人永远不会支持我，无论我说什么或做什么。这是他们的选择。但我正在与那些不仅了解我是一名运动员，而且了解我是丈夫和一个小女儿的父亲的人交谈。
在战斗周之前和期间，我的对手提起了我大学时代的一件事。我相信它被提出来是为了进入我的脑海，但它也重新开启了多年前就已经解决的问题。
我想明确一点：我没有做任何被指控的事情。我从未被指控犯罪，这件事最终被地方检察官撤销。这些指控既没有被忽视，也没有被置之不理。在我与执法部门充分合作的过程中，他们受到了彻底和严格的审查，包括单独的第九条审查。
没有刑事指控，没有定罪，也没有对我的责任认定。这件事已经结束，也没有涉及我的未决法律问题。我自己的律师进行了自己的调查，并在记录中表示，即使法律发生了变化，我也会有同样的结果，这现在证明了

articles.summary_zh: HHS取消了760000名参加healthcare.gov计划的个人的健康保险
articles.content_orig:
HHS cancels health insurance of 760,000 individuals enrolled in healthcare.gov plans
The Department of Health and Human Services announced something it's never done before - canceled the health insurance of 760,000 individuals enrolled in plans in the Affordable Care Act marketplace.
Today, the Department of Health and Human Services announced it had done something it has never done before. It canceled the health insurance of 760,000 people enrolled in plans in the Affordable Care Act Marketplace, also known as healthcare.gov. NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin is here to tell us more. Hi.
SELENA SIMMONS-DUFFIN, BYLINE: Hi, Juana.
SUMMERS: So, Selena, I understand that Vice President JD Vance held a press conference today.
SIMMONS-DUFFIN: Yeah, that's right. It was under the auspice of the White House anti-fraud task force led by Vance. He was talking about the federal health insurance marketplace, also known as Obamacare, and just as a reminder, this is for people who don't get insurance from their job or a public program like Medicare or Medicaid. They can go on healthcare.gov and buy a private health insurance plan, oftentimes with premium subsidies paid for by the federal government. So today, Vice President Vance said that fraudster brokers were signing up, quote, "phantom people" into these plans. Here's Vance.
(SOUNDBITE OF PRESS CONFERENCE)
JD VANCE: You have a system where, on the one hand, brokers are paid money to feed patients into the system, while on the other hand, the government isn't even checking whether the people enrolled are actually eligible for the program. What do you have? - of course, rampant, rampant fraud.
SIMMONS-DUFFIN: So he put the blame on brokers for committing the fraud and announced moves to punish them, like stopping new brokers from registering for the upcoming open enrollment and changing enrollment processes. He said the government would save more than $2 billion in subsidies they would have been sending to insurance companies for those enrollments that they canceled.
SUMMERS: Interesting. So did the officials explain their process for identifying these enrollments as fraudulent?

articles.title_orig: Major hurricane Polo intensifies off Mexico's Pacific coast
articles.title_zh: 飓风波罗在墨西哥太平洋沿岸加剧
articles.summary_zh: 飓风波罗是一个强大的5级飓风，周二在墨西哥海岸附近的太平洋经历了极端快速的增强。
articles.content_orig:
Hurricane Polo is a powerful Category 5 after undergoing extreme rapid intensification Tuesday in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Mexico.
⛈️ Check your local forecast and learn more about hurricanes in the CNN Weather app
The hurricane’s sustained winds rocketed to 180 mph Tuesday afternoon – tying a pair of super typhoons in the West Pacific for the strongest storm on the planet so far this year. Polo is feeding off of a favorable atmosphere and warmer water driven by the super El Niño, which is fueling a hyperactive hurricane season across the Pacific. More hurricanes are also rapidly intensifying as Earth and its oceans warm from fossil fuel pollution.
Extreme rapid intensification is a wind increase of 58 mph or more in 24 hours. Polo met that criteria and then some, with a wind increase of 110 mph, going from a 50 mph tropical storm to a 160 mph Category 5 from Monday to Tuesday morning.
This rate of rapid intensification is “truly remarkable,” the National Hurricane Center said Tuesday morning, and is among the fastest on record in the Eastern Pacific.
Hurricane Patricia set the Eastern Pacific 24-hour intensification record in 2015 when its winds jumped 120 mph. Polo is comparable to 2023’s Hurricane Otis, which had a wind increase of 105 mph in 21 hours before slamming into and devastating Acapulco, Mexico.
Polo was a few hundred miles south-southeast of Manzanillo, Mexico, on Tuesday. Its dangerous hurricane-force winds are forecast to remain offshore as it moves northwestward parallel to the Mexican coastline through the end of the week.
The powerful hurricane was moving southeastward, but it’s expected to turn to the northwest on Tuesday night.
Tropical storm alerts are in effect for Mexico’s southwestern coast since this area is expected to see tropical storm conditions by early Wednesday. Heavy rain is Polo’s most significant impact and it could cause life-threatening flooding and mudslides in this region.
Rainfall totals in Guerrero and Michoacán states could reach 3 to 6 inches, with locally up to 8 inches in spots through Thursday. Coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima and Jalisco states could receive 2 to 4 inches of rain.
articles.content_zh:
飓风波罗是一个强大的5级飓风，周二在墨西哥海岸附近的太平洋经历了极端快速的增强。
⛈️ 查看您当地的天气预报，并在CNN天气应用程序中了解更多关于飓风的信息
周二下午，飓风的持续风速飙升至每小时180英里，与西太平洋的两个超级台风并列，成为今年迄今为止地球上最强的风暴。波罗正在从超级厄尔尼诺现象驱动的有利大气和温暖的海水中汲取营养，这加剧了太平洋地区极度活跃的飓风季节。随着地球及其海洋因化石燃料污染而变暖，更多的飓风也在迅速加剧。
极端快速增强是指24小时内风速增加58英里/小时或以上。波罗满足了这一标准，然后在周一至周二上午，风速增加了110英里/小时，从50英里/小时的热带风暴上升到160英里/小时5级。
国家飓风中心周二上午表示，这种快速加剧的速度“确实非常显著”，是东太平洋有记录以来最快的速度之一。
2015年，飓风帕特里夏创下了东太平洋24小时强化记录，风速达到每小时120英里。波罗相当于2023年的飓风奥蒂斯，在21小时内风速增加了105英里/小时，然后猛烈袭击并摧毁了墨西哥阿卡普尔科。
周二，波罗在墨西哥曼萨尼约东南偏南几百英里处。预计其危险的飓风强度风将在本周末沿墨西哥海岸线向西北方向移动，并保持在近海。
强飓风正在向东南移动，但预计周二晚上将转向西北。
墨西哥西南海岸的热带风暴警报已经生效，因为预计该地区将在周三早些时候出现热带风暴。大雨是波罗最严重的影响，可能会在该地区造成危及生命的洪水和泥石流。
格雷罗州和米却肯州的总降雨量可能达到3至6英寸，截至周四，当地降雨量可达8英寸。瓦哈卡州、科利马州和哈利斯科州的沿海地区可能会迎来2至4英寸的降雨。

articles.title_orig: Nolan Wells' parents make plea for justice after no charges filed in his death - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Nolan Wells' parents make plea for justice after no charges filed in his death - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Nolan Wells' parents make plea for justice after no charges filed in his death
The parents and attorneys discussed the grand jury report on Tuesday.
Nolan Wells' family and their attorneys said they will not give up on finding justice a day after a grand jury found that no criminal charges are warranted in his death, they said at a press conference on Tuesday.
The 18-year-old vanished after he and friends had gone out celebrating the Fourth of July holiday on barrier islands off the Gulf Coast of Mississippi. His body was recovered in the waters off Horn Island two days later.
The Mississippi State medical examiner performed the initial autopsy on Wells' body. The teen's family commissioned a private autopsy before results from the state autopsy were released.
The grand jury that reviewed the evidence in Wells’ death found unanimously that therethat there was insufficient evidence to bring criminal charges in the case, according to the Jackson County Grand Jury Report.
The report said that the "position of, condition of, time of discovery, and location" of the 18-year-old's body off the coast of Mississippi this July is "consistent with drowning."
The report also said there was no credible evidence of criminal conduct by the friends, who are white, who traveled with him to an island off the Mississippi coast on July 4.
The grand jury heard from 43 witnesses and reviewed materials including physical evidence collected at the scene, the state medical examiner's autopsy, digital evidence, police reports and interviews, videos, images and maps collected during the investigation.
But the family questioned the conclusion of the grand jury report.
"Please remember that both medical examiners, as well as his death certificates, states that the cause and manner of his death is undetermined," Christine Wonsley, Wells' mother, said at the press conference. "So, my question is: How can a jury come to the conclusion of drowning, despite knowing that there was trauma to his body?"
"Later, the independent autopsy conducted for the family by forensic pathologist Dr. Roger A. Mitchell Jr. found that Nolan sustained recent, unexplained blunt force injuries to the back of his head and additional areas on his back," the family attorney said.
The grand jury's report however found that the bruising on the back of Wells' head was "not a fatal injury" and it was unclear how he got it.
One witness testified under oath that around the time of his last being seen, they saw Wells "slip awkwardly off the side of a boat" but "could not say whether Mr. Wells struck his head during the fall," and that he "continued to socialize after the fall and did not appear injured," according to the grand jury report.
The state medical examiner has not released their official autopsy, but the grand jury report said that the "position of, condition of, time of discovery, and location" of Wells' body off the coast of Mississippi this July is "consistent with drowning."
The grand jury of 23 people, convened last week, found "no credible evidence to support the public allegations" that anyone riding to or from the island that day surrounding Wells "engaged in any criminal conduct related to" his death.
That Wells drowned is a conclusion by the process of elimination, the grand jury report said, adding that the condition of the body made it harder to figure out.
At the press conference, the family's attorneys said that they will have the opportunity to reopen the investigation in a civil case."He deserved to be at school right now," Wonsley, Wells' mother, said. "We should be getting text messages and phone calls. But most importantly, Nolan deserved to live. At the end of the day, there is only one victim, and it is our son, Nolan Xavier Wells."
The grand jury report said Wells' family was given the opportunity to produce evidence from their private investigation into Wells' death and the family's lawyers advised that their investigation "revealed no witnesses or evidence whom the legal team reasonably believes possess information germane to potential criminal activity that warrants referral."
It also noted that there is no statute of limitations on homicide cases in Mississippi.
"If credible evidence comes to light in the future that suggests Mr. Wells' death was non-accidental, this matter should be represented to the Jackson County Grand Jury for further consideration," the report said.
ABC News' Sabina Ghebremedhin, Synai Ferrell and Sasha Pezenik contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: US supreme court declines to intervene in custody fight over baby born via surrogate
articles.title_zh: US supreme court declines to intervene in custody fight over baby born via surrogate
articles.content_orig:
The supreme court has refused to get involved with a custody dispute between an Alaska surrogate and a California couple whose child was born with a rare and serious heart defect.
On Tuesday, Justice Elena Kagan denied an emergency request from McKenna West, an Alaska nurse and surrogate who had asked the US’s highest court to halt a California court order recognizing the couple, Omar Ahmed and Nausheen Gilkar, as the boy’s legal parents.
In recent weeks, the case has garnered nationwide attention, sparking broader discussions about surrogacy and abortion.
In a 9 September filing, West’s attorneys urged the supreme court to intervene in what they described as “extraordinary circumstances”, arguing that “a life hangs in the balance”.
Following a scan that discovered the baby having hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a condition that impedes blood flow and requires extensive surgery, Ahmed and Gilkar asked West to abort the pregnancy. According to NBC, the couple signed a contract last August with West that included a clause stating that the pregnancy could be terminated in the case of a “fetal abnormality”.
However, West refused to terminate the pregnancy and instead traveled to Texas, where abortion is illegal, to give birth. Republican attorney general Ken Paxton intervened, shining a national spotlight on the case. A Dallas judge subsequently issued an order requiring the baby to receive medical care.
Kagan’s refusal to intervene comes just days after the Texas supreme court ruled that the month-old child can leave Texas and relocate to a Los Angeles hospital for treatment.
“Sustaining the life of the medically fragile child is the paramount concern in this time-sensitive matter,” the court said.
West has since argued for custody of the child, claiming that his legal parents will not provide the necessary medical care because they had previously sought an abortion.
West’s attorneys say that because their client “is now completely excluded from the life of the medically fragile infant she brought into the world, much less from the ability to make critical health decisions that protect him, time is of the essence”.
In West’s filing to the supreme court, her lawyers argued that “without relief, she will receive no further information about the child she carried for 37 weeks and fought to save”.
During a court hearing in Dallas last month, the child’s parents said West was “unstable”. Gilkar added: “He’s our child … He’s the most beautiful person I’ve never seen … He’s the love of our lives. He’s suffering a lot.”

articles.title_orig: Kratom found at locations where two Ole Miss students were discovered dead
articles.title_zh: Kratom在发现两名Ole Miss学生死亡的地点发现了尸体
articles.summary_zh: 执法官员周二表示，密西西比大学的两名学生本周死亡，在单独的死亡调查中发现了包装好的kratom。
articles.content_orig:
Two University of Mississippi students died this week and packaged kratom was found during the separate death investigations, law enforcement officials said Tuesday.
Authorities said they have not confirmed that kratom or any other substance was a contributing factor in either death.
Lafayette County Metro Narcotics said Tuesday that it has no information that the two deaths are linked.
“However, packaged Kratom sold from a retail store was found during both investigations,” it said in a statement. “Out of an abundance of caution, we encourage everyone to avoid kratom and any other medication or substance that was not prescribed to you or obtained from a trusted, regulated source.”
The Ole Miss students have not been publicly identified by authorities.
Both were found dead Monday; one on campus, and the other in the city of Oxford, Mayor Robyn Tannehill said.
“The University is heartbroken by the recent loss of two students and extends our condolences to their families, friends, and loved ones during this difficult time,” the university said.
The deaths, which are under investigation by local, state and federal authorities, are being treated as separate inquiries, according to Lafayette County Metro Narcotics.
Raegan Settle, a senior who is the student editor-in-chief of the student newspaper “The Daily Mississippian,” said the mood on campus was “really frantic.” A lot of the details were just coming out Tuesday, she said.
“Many students are hanging black ribbons around their sorority and fraternity houses as we speak,” she said. “So, I think people are just really shocked.”
Greek organizations on campus have been reminding members not to take anything that is not prescribed specifically for them by their doctor, Settle said.
Kratom, the name of a product and the Southeast Asia tree from which it comes, has gained popularity in the U.S. as an unapproved treatment for pain, anxiety and drug dependence. It is sometimes sold at gas stations or online.
Kratom can produce either stimulating or sedating effects, depending on the dosage taken, and can produce psychotic symptoms, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration.
It’s not federally banned, but the DEA lists it as a “drug and chemical of concern.” The Mayo Clinic calls kratom unsafe and ineffective and says it’s been linked to a small number of deaths, but that “nearly all deaths from kratom also involved other drugs or substances.”
Kratom has been banned by local laws in Oxford, Mississippi, but can be bought in surrounding counties, said Capt. Alex Fauver, commander of the Metro Narcotics unit.
“We have a lot of problems with the kratom and people on it, it has no medical use,” he said in a phone interview.
Kratom was found at each student’s residence, he said.
There have been no other student deaths and no other students or members of the community impacted, Fauver and the university said.
Authorities urged people not to speculate, and acknowledged that there was unverified information being spread online.
Lafayette County Metro Narcotics said there was a “significant amount of concern, speculation, and misinformation circulating.”

The Nasdaq Composite rose to a fresh all-time intraday high on Tuesday, while the S&P 500 was relatively unchanged as traders continued to keep an eye on developments between the U.S. and Iran.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq climbed 0.45% to a record close of 27,244.28, supported by a nearly 7% gain in shares of Sandisk following a bullish call from Rosenblatt. The S&P 500 was marginally lower at 7,764.64, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 185.14 points, or 0.36%, to end at 51,863.69.
Oil prices moved lower after President Donald Trump said that U.S. officials had a "very good meeting" with Iran's delegation and that it lasted about three hours. Global benchmark Brent crude futures settled down 1.09% at $99.25 per barrel. U.S. crude futures traded 1.24% lower to settle at $94.59 a barrel. That marked the fifth straight day of losses for both benchmarks.
Addressing the United Nations General Assembly Tuesday, Trump said that he has a "big decision" to make on whether to pursue a deal with Iran or "annihilate" the country.
He also said that he believes "we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to," adding that "they're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election."
Oil had fallen earlier in the day after Iran reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. To be sure, the reports have not been independently verified by CNBC. Saudi Arabia is also reportedly planning to restart its East-West pipeline as early as this week.
Tuesday's moves follow a strong session on Wall Street, with the S&P 500 posting its best day since Aug. 4 and the Nasdaq notching its first closing record since June.
A decline in oil prices fueled the stock market's gains, while Treasury yields pulled back as well. articles.summary_zh: 当辛迪·克劳馥27岁的儿子普雷斯利·格伯周日在加利福尼亚州的一家康复中心去世的消息传出时，人们开始质疑，一个能够获得广泛治疗资源的人怎么可能仍然会因成瘾而失去生命。
articles.content_orig:
When news broke that Presley Gerber, the 27-year-old son of Cindy Crawford, died Sunday at a California rehab facility, it raised questions about how someone with access to extensive treatment resources could still lose his life to addiction.
According to addiction specialist Dr. Drew Pinsky, Gerber’s case highlights the deadly, progressive nature of substance use disorder — and what he says is a dangerous trend in modern treatment: allowing patients to dictate their own care.
"When I listened to [Gerber's] video, what struck me and concerned me was that the patient seemed to be determining some of the care," Pinsky said on his podcast, "Ask Dr. Drew." "That's never good."
PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY
Pinsky discussed Gerber’s self-reported trip to Mexico for an "ibogaine flood," referring to a high-dose treatment involving ibogaine, a psychoactive compound derived from an African shrub that has been studied as a potential treatment for substance use disorders but is not approved by the FDA.
"I've had patients using ibogaine or ayahuasca for decades, and there's nothing magic about it, I assure you," Pinsky warned, noting that almost every patient he’s seen try the alternative drug eventually relapsed on opioids, often suffering personality changes in the process.
Ibogaine remains an unapproved Schedule I substance in the U.S. due to documented risks of fatal heart arrhythmias, according to federal health agencies.
BRAD PITT SAYS HE CAN DRINK IN ‘RESTRAINED MANNER’ AFTER 7 SOBER YEARS, BUT EXPERT RAISES RED FLAG
Pinsky argued that Gerber’s case highlights how patients struggling with severe substance use disorder are often allowed to bypass proven medical protocols in favor of risky alternative therapies.

Addressing public shock that the young model died inside a treatment center, Pinsky emphasized that high-end rehab centers cannot magically halt severe opioid dependence.
"Opioid addiction is progressive and it ends in death," Pinsky said. "Even with good treatment, it has a worse prognosis than most cancers ... If they are not moving toward recovery, they are moving toward demise."
